I believe students should create their own summer project designs because they can develop very imaginative ideas, enjoy the process more, and experience less pressure during the summer break.

Students have the opportunity to produce innovative projects by exploring various experiments or researching the lives of interesting people. For example, a student might find exciting science experiments to perform, which could be both educational and enjoyable for themselves and their classmates. Alternatively, they could choose to study a famous person or a family member and explain why they selected that individual. This allows students to invent original projects, present their ideas to the class, and describe how their creation could be useful to themselves or others.

Creating their own projects can make the experience more enjoyable for students. They are likely to be more enthusiastic when working on something they have designed themselves, rather than simply completing an assignment given to the entire class. With the freedom to explore, students often produce more imaginative results and can find pleasure in a task that is not limited by strict instructions. Additionally, students may have the chance to collaborate with friends, making the project even more fun.

Finally, designing their own summer projects can help students feel less stressed. They can work without worrying about making their project perfect or strictly following a set list of requirements. Instead, students can create their own goals and later share their process with classmates, inspiring others to try similar projects for enjoyment.

In summary, these are the reasons why I think students should have the freedom to design their own summer projects.

Individuals should take responsibility for their own choices rather than relying too heavily on advice from so-called "experts."

First of all, people are the best judges of what suits them because they understand their own preferences and needs, both mentally and physically. For instance, if someone buys a gift for another person without knowing their tastes or needs, it is likely that the gift will be unwanted or inappropriate. This shows that relying on someone else to decide for you can often lead to mistakes.

Often, they end up with items that don’t fit properly. This experience can teach them to measure themselves or visit a store before purchasing clothes online in the future. Another example is when people buy something that looks appealing online but do not read the full description, only to find the item is different from the picture, smaller than expected, or missing parts. Such experiences help them become more careful consumers.

For example, someone might pay a lawyer a large sum of money, only to lose their case. Similarly, a patient might visit a doctor for pain, only to be told they are fine and prescribed costly medication they may not actually need. Therapists sometimes prescribe medicine unnecessarily as well, depending on their personal approach. This shows that even experts can make mistakes or may have financial motives.

In conclusion, because experts do not always have the right answers, and because making mistakes is a natural part of learning, it is often better for people to make their own decisions. This ensures they avoid poor advice and develop better judgment over time.

Some people ask if it is better to work with a group or alone? Everyone has different opinions about the benefits of working in a group or working alone, some people prefer working alone and others prefer working in groups. I believe that the best way for the people to improve is by working in groups because they learn more and understand better.

Each group learn something new from each other.

"Everyday we all learn new things in life".

Second, working in groups help the people improve because they will understand better. For example, asking their partners if they have a question or didn't understand really well. "We could do more if we all help each others".

Even though some people say the opposite, i believe that working in groups is better than working alone.

People often wonder whether it is better to work independently or collaborate within a group. Opinions on this topic vary, as some individuals enjoy working by themselves, while others prefer teamwork. In my opinion, working in groups is the most effective way to grow, since it allows people to learn more and gain a deeper understanding.

Firstly, group work encourages improvement in both academic and professional settings because it exposes individuals to new ideas. For instance, hearing different perspectives from teammates can broaden one’s knowledge. I remember one day in my English class when the teacher divided us into groups of four and handed each group a sheet of paper. Then, he wrote several questions on the board and instructed us to answer them together. After we finished, each group shared their responses with the class. We noticed that every group had its unique opinions and viewpoints, and we all learned something different from one another.

Secondly, collaborating in groups enhances comprehension. If someone is unclear about a topic, they can ask their peers for clarification. For example, in my history class, the teacher assigned us a task to complete during the lesson. When the instructions were unclear to me, I asked a classmate to explain it again so I could fully understand, contribute my ideas, and support my group’s work.

On the other hand, some argue that working alone is better because it helps with concentration. They believe that individual work prevents distractions and allows quicker completion of tasks. A friend of mine prefers working alone, saying that group work often leads to chatting, distractions, and less work accomplished. However, this reasoning is flawed because when people work alone and don’t fully grasp the assignment, they lack the chance to have someone explain it to them. As a result, they might get stuck and not finish their work. Having others to discuss problems with can be very helpful.

In conclusion, working in groups brings many advantages. Besides learning new information, group work helps build friendships, discover more about others, and understand oneself better. Collaborating with others is beneficial because it reduces pressure about finishing tasks on time and provides support when needing guidance. Although some people claim otherwise, I firmly believe that working with a group is superior to working alone.

At times, a little help from others is what we need to grow and improve.

Providing students with the option to attend classes from home through online platforms or video conferencing may seem like a good idea, but I believe that students do not truly benefit from this method of learning for several reasons.

To begin with, many students struggle to focus when learning remotely. They are often distracted by their phones or other electronic gadgets, which they tend to use frequently. Additionally, disturbances from family members, such as parents or siblings, can interrupt their concentration and cause them to fall behind in their studies. These distractions can lead to delays in completing coursework and ultimately result in poor academic performance. For example, my cousin moved to the United States with his siblings and was allowed to take one course online. However, he often found it difficult to concentrate at home due to the noise and interruptions from his family, and this negatively affected his grades, causing him to fail the course.

Another issue is that some students find learning at their own pace unengaging and challenging. Without a teacher physically present to explain difficult concepts, students may struggle to grasp the material. Distance learning can feel monotonous because it lacks interactive discussions and real-time feedback, which many students find motivating. Some learners prefer an active learning environment rather than working alone and passively. As a result, they might skip lessons or simply stop engaging with the content altogether. I had a friend who experienced similar difficulties; he found it boring and hard to follow online classes. Despite trying to stay awake by drinking strong coffee, he would often turn off his computer and go to bed, which hurt his academic success.

Finally, fatigue is a common problem for students in distance learning setups because they may not have enough rest between their daily activities and online lessons. Some students also have jobs after traditional school hours before attending their online classes, leaving them exhausted and less focused. I have personally experienced this myself. After school, I have to walk a significant distance home, complete my assignments, and take a shower before starting my online classes late at night. This makes me feel tired and sometimes weak, which affects my ability to learn effectively.

In conclusion, I believe that students do not gain much from distance learning due to several drawbacks that can lower their academic achievement. The distractions, lack of interaction, and fatigue involved in remote education make it less effective for many students.

It is important to spend quality time together and visit places you both enjoy. Their behavior might improve because they may just need someone to listen or to spend time with. Everyone has a unique personality, and sometimes you need to accept those differences.

Moreover, people often go through difficult times that affect their personality. Asking someone how they feel can reveal if they are feeling sad or upset and simply need someone to talk to. Being there for each other and offering support can make a big difference.

In summary, the saying "Don't judge a book by its cover" reminds us that we never truly know the reasons behind someone's behavior. Even if you don’t know someone well, ask if they are alright. It is definitely possible to influence their personality in a positive way and help them become a better person.

Some schools permit the use of cell phones in classrooms for educational purposes. Many people support the idea that having phones can benefit students academically. However, I disagree and think students should not have phones in class because they can easily become distracted, miss out on effective learning opportunities, and because using a phone should be considered a privilege.

The first reason I oppose cell phones in classrooms is that they can divert students' attention. Instead of focusing on the lesson or the tasks assigned by the teacher, students might use their phones for non-educational activities such as texting or browsing social media. This can cause them to lose concentration and fail to complete their academic work properly. Over time, they may also develop the habit of thinking it is acceptable to use phones during learning time.

Secondly, having phones in class reduces the chance for students to experience traditional learning methods. Those who take notes by hand tend to remember information better and perform well on tests. Additionally, when lessons involve interactive or hands-on activities, students can deepen their understanding and even help each other learn, which is less likely to happen if phones are a constant distraction.

Finally, phones should be treated as a privilege rather than a right during class time. Teachers should restrict phone use because students might struggle to know when it is appropriate to use them. Even with strict rules, many students will find ways to bypass restrictions and use their phones when they should be focusing on their studies.

In summary, I believe phones should not be allowed in classrooms because they cause distractions, hinder learning, and should be considered a privilege. Schools ought to prevent students from using their phones while lessons are in progress.

Haile G/Selasie, one of the most famous long distance runners of all time, did not pave his way to success because he was born with it. He came from a poor family, and walked a long distance to his school everyday. When he started running, he was not good at all. He worked day and night to get to where he is. And when he speaks about his past, he tells the story of how he failed again and again a lot of times but he never lost his passion for his dream. And now he is one of the richest people in Ethiopia and one of the best record holders of Marathon.

Success is a dream for most and a reality for only a few. When it comes to how success is achieved, it creates a great question in all our minds and that is,"How can I be successful?". Some say that success is achieved by going through failures without giving up or without losing hope. That is a truly arguable idea and some might think different. But I fully agree with that idea.

The fact that almost all of the masterminds that are known for their creations of the bulb, physics theories, telephone and many more of the things we take for granted at the moment told the story of how they tried and failed many times than they count. And that is one proof of the point that success doesn't come without failure.

There might be some people that argue this point by pointing out that many people have tried and failed and tried again but it didn't help them achieve their dreams. That is a good point but the fact is that failing is not the only thing that determines your success, but failing and not being discouraged is what really counts. If we plan to achieve a goal, we shouldn't lose our excitement for that specific thing we're doing, we should rather be more encouraged to try harder and to find another way to make it work.

For example, when we first built a rocket,it wasn't done in a day or in the first try. Engineers tried to fix the problem in the mechanical part. Scientists tried to see if their calculations was wrong or if the combination of the chemicals didn't work and many others tried to fix it but they failed more than a couple of times. By not giving up though, it was a success at last.

It might not always seem like it but failure leads to success. The main point is not giving up and not losing our enthusiasm. As the saying goes, "If you fail once, try and try harder". Never give up on your dreams and don't be discouraged by failure.

A valuable tip to avoid problems is to “think before you speak.” Failing to do so can result in many unwanted consequences.

A trip to the Bahamas would help me reduce stress and broaden my understanding of different cultures and languages.

The Bahamas could support this goal because it has wide, safe streets, which some places lack. I would be able to bike all around the city without worrying about traffic accidents.

Have you ever wondered what life is like in the Bahamas?

I would like to live there, although it is pricey, just like many other places. Living costs vary depending on factors such as food, views, and lifestyle, with some locations being more affordable than others. Some residents stay in the Bahamas despite the high costs because they may have well-paying jobs or come from wealthy families. Living by the beach can be difficult due to its high expense and risks from storms and other natural disasters. Therefore, I prefer to live further inland for safety reasons. The Bahamas’ vast array of colorful plants and animals is another reason why it appeals to me.

In summary, the Bahamas is one of the most vibrant and beautiful places in the world, offering a wealth of activities, talents to develop, and cultural experiences. This is why I want to visit the Bahamas.

However, many students favor group work because it allows them to divide tasks, exchange ideas, and support each other. Collaborating in a team often leads to greater efficiency. For these reasons, I believe that working in groups is more advantageous for students.

To begin with, students frequently have numerous projects to complete each grading period, which can be overwhelming, especially when a major project counts for 10% of the overall grade. By working in a group, the project can be divided among members, making the workload more manageable. Each student possesses unique skills that can be applied to specific parts of the project, making tasks easier for everyone involved.

Moreover, group work offers students a valuable chance to develop cooperation skills. Many companies assign tasks to teams rather than individuals because combining diverse knowledge and abilities improves results. Businesses often encourage employees to “work as a team” to boost productivity. Teachers should recognize this and use group projects to prepare students for real-world teamwork, while also helping them learn from one another.

In addition, collaborating in groups can increase students’ confidence. When students discuss topics together, they can explore different approaches and choose the best methods. Schools often allow students to stay after class, which benefits those who cannot meet at a group member’s home. Group work also supports students who struggle with meeting deadlines, as peers can provide assistance and encourage more consistent progress.

In summary, no student should face a major project alone without the option to work in a group. Since many companies rely on teams to complete tasks more effectively, teachers should adopt a similar approach in the classroom to help students improve their grades and submit work on time. Allowing group work not only enhances teamwork skills but also offers multiple perspectives that contribute to better outcomes in any subject.

When was the last time you put your phone down and really looked up at the sky? Nowadays, the first thing most people do after waking up is reach for their phones. We rely on technology every day; it has become a part of our lives. While technology keeps advancing and changing rapidly, are we growing along with it? We often invest so much of our lives online, comparing ourselves to others. It’s no surprise that many people feel unhappy, focusing on what others have rather than appreciating their own blessings. Although everyone sees the same things, their perspectives are different.

One major issue is the amount of time wasted on screens. People’s attention is constantly fixed on their personal devices. Many just follow the trends without thinking — caring more about the latest news, the newest products, or gossip. Self-interest seems to dominate, where people are preoccupied with their phones and brands like Supreme. They compete for likes and online fame, creating fake images of themselves on social media. They often express negativity through calls or video chats but hesitate to confront others face-to-face. There’s a fear of not fitting in or lacking the newest, biggest, or most expensive items, believing that higher cost means more value. This obsession with screens affects both the mind and body. Many develop poor posture, often slouching with curved backs. Back problems have become increasingly common. Personally, I have struggled with back pain from spending too much time hunched over as a child. It seems like eventually, those who stand tall with straight backs will be the leaders, because it’s impossible to hold a strong presence when you’re bent over.

Technology certainly has its benefits. It can help us finish homework, connect with others, find love, or even discover new places to live. Technology itself isn’t bad—people just misuse and abuse it. While it offers many advantages, it can also cause harm, and many fail to recognize this dual impact.

Winston Churchill’s statement holds great significance in American life today. Many people who experience failure find the strength to get back up and continue pursuing their goals. However, some believe that when they fail, they should give up and stop trying altogether. It is important to consider both perspectives. Churchill’s message encourages us to persist and not quit.

One key reason to keep going is that failure teaches us valuable lessons. When you fail, it’s essential to realize that it’s not the end of the journey. Making mistakes helps you understand what to do differently next time. Recognizing this can motivate you to keep aiming for success. Standing firm in your beliefs and working hard towards your goals is always the right path.

Another reason to never give up is the desire to achieve your highest ambitions. If there is something you truly want, you must keep striving for it. Many who fail or make errors tend to give up, thinking they have wasted their time. However, life is not about winning every time or doing everything perfectly. Everyone faces setbacks at some point, and although failing is discouraging, we continue pushing ahead because we want to succeed and feel proud that we didn’t quit.

On the other hand, giving up often leads to failure in the long run. Those who believe they can achieve good jobs, attend excellent schools, or realize their dreams without setbacks are usually the ones who give up as soon as they encounter failure. People who have succeeded in their careers or education got there through hard work and perseverance. Even when times were tough, they didn’t stop because they remained focused on their goals. It’s common for people who fail to say they aren’t smart or good enough. But if that were true, how did they get this far? When you struggle, remember that the people around you—friends and family—can support you and help you overcome challenges.

In conclusion, whenever you have a goal or something important you want to accomplish, it is crucial not to give up halfway. A goal is something you desire, and through effort, you can reach it eventually. When problems arise or you feel stuck, there are always people ready to support you. By refusing to quit, you can build confidence in yourself and face life’s challenges with determination.

A single persons actions can change how other people act. Albert Schweitzer, a philosopher said, "Example is not the main thing in influencing others; it is the only thing". I agree with his statement and believe it as true, as most people look up to and copy whoever is currently popular on social media. People also like to follow the example of what they are taught, by parents or teachers. In this essay, i'll be talking about how setting an example for others is the best way to influence others into doing something.

First of all, Watching someone do something that interests you could influence you into doing the same. For example: if you like food and you watch someone cook, it could possibly persuade you into making your own food. Most of the time, people would not do something without being influenced or persuaded by someone else. Take Juuling for example, most kids would never do such a thing unless being persuaded or peer pressured by their friends.

Secondly, Teaching someone to do good by an example is also good, as it sets them down a good path, just as most parents do. A person cant do something they were never taught or ever learned, so they look to other people who can do things; and look up to them. Only by setting an example can others follow. Much like a pack of wolves, the leader sets an example and rest follow it.

It could be argued that a speech or something of the sort could also influence people, such as Martin Luther King Jr's "I Have A Dream" speech. In the past that might have been the best way to influence people, but in modern day society a majority of people are influenced by action and examples. Otherwise, why would kids be doing these "Challenges" that you hear on the news every other day?

In conclusion, Examples are the best and most effective way to influence others into doing things. By setting examples, people are influenced into doing all sorts of things. Whether they are good or bad is completely subjective and depends on what the person is influenced into doing.

It is beneficial for students to decide on a career early in life because they will gain a clearer understanding of what the job involves, discover enjoyable activities to engage in daily, and avoid future worries about career choices as adults.

They might not fully grasp what the job requires or understand the basic responsibilities involved. To gain this knowledge, it is important for students to have hands-on experiences or early exposure to the profession. Getting involved allows them to learn firsthand about patient care and other duties. Besides direct experience, students can also research careers they find interesting. For instance, a student curious about dentistry can easily find information about the steps needed to become a dentist. By exploring career options early, students can access many resources that guide them toward their goals.

Many students don’t engage in meaningful activities after school or during their free time. Those who remain inactive often feel bored or unhappy. Participating in career-related programs or activities after school can offer students both education and enjoyment. Many students struggle to find hobbies or interests that keep them motivated and satisfied. Exploring careers can help them discover activities they truly enjoy, which can serve as fulfilling hobbies.

Additionally, choosing a career early can eliminate future stress about job decisions. Many teenagers are unsure about what they want to do when they grow up. This uncertainty often leads to difficulties in securing employment later on. However, students who invest time early on in learning about a career will have a clearer sense of direction. They will find it easier to choose a job and will experience less anxiety about their future. When students graduate from high school, they commonly face pressure to find a job, which causes stress. Those who have already explored their interests and career options tend to feel more confident and less worried during this time.

For students who are uncertain about their future careers, spending time on research and joining career-focused programs can provide valuable guidance. Early involvement in career exploration reduces stress and helps students make better-informed decisions.

Unfortunately, these students often face more challenges when looking for work later. To fully understand a profession, students need to take part in career fairs or gain exposure to the field itself. Early commitment to a career allows students to be better prepared and more informed. Moreover, it helps them find enjoyable interests and prevents future worries related to employment. For these reasons, students should begin considering their career paths at a young age.

Energy and resources are essential elements for human development and survival. Various kinds of resources exist, including money, materials, and energy itself. These resources have supported human life for centuries and continue to do so today. Everyone in the world should be responsible for conserving them, as they play a crucial role in sustaining our way of life. Unfortunately, many people neglect this duty, either because they are unaware of the consequences or simply ignore the issue. It is important to correct this neglect and protect our resources. This essay will discuss advice, advantages, disadvantages, and strategies for conserving our resources.

Let’s consider the advantages we can gain by saving resources. One suggestion is to introduce a four-day workweek, with each workday lasting ten hours and school days limited to two hours. This plan could help protect the environment by lowering pollution rates and preserve resources for critical situations. If we implement this system, problems might arise, such as losing valuable learning time in schools and work hours in jobs. Our social interactions at school and work could decrease, and becoming an expert in any field might become more difficult and slower. Technological progress could also be hindered, which would impact human advancement. Consequently, we risk losing important opportunities and resources that make life easier and more efficient.

In conclusion, while many people could benefit from this plan, it would also bring certain challenges and drawbacks. If we decide to adopt it, we must be aware of the risks involved and work to minimize any negative effects. Instead of wasting time, we should focus on creating a better world with a sustainable lifestyle and develop projects to conserve resources. Governments should take the lead in implementing such initiatives since they have the authority to manage a country. They are essential for our survival and for maintaining the quality of life we have in the twenty-first century.

Learning from home through online classes or videoconferencing is not an ideal method for students, as it cannot fully replace the experience they gain by attending school in person. If remote learning becomes a regular practice, students may miss out on forming meaningful friendships with their peers and building connections with their teachers. Moreover, studying at home often leads students to take their education less seriously than they would in a school setting, where teachers, counselors, and administrators provide guidance and encouragement.

Firstly, attending classes remotely differs greatly from being physically present at school. At school, students tend to approach their homework, quizzes, and exams with more dedication than they might from home. When students are physically in the classroom, they can easily ask questions about the subject matter and receive clear explanations and examples from their teachers. Additionally, being at school allows students to seek extra help after class, retake tests if needed, or study together with peers in learning centers. These opportunities are typically unavailable when students attend online classes. As a result, students’ academic performance may decline because they do not have the same level of support to clarify their doubts or solve difficulties.

Secondly, if online classes become the norm, students will lose the chance to develop strong communication skills and build social relationships. In a school environment, students can exchange ideas, share concerns, and enjoy social interactions during breaks or lunch. Often, classmates become friends or even resemble a supportive family, making school feel like a second home where students find both academic and personal support. Conversely, learning online from home can be isolating and boring, as students lack classmates to talk to or collaborate with. Furthermore, many teenagers today face mental health challenges like stress, anxiety, and depression; being at school helps them distract from their issues and provides access to counselors, teachers, and friends who can offer advice and support. Overall, school offers a supportive community that is difficult to replicate in an online setting.

Finally, online learning may not be effective for students who struggle with self-discipline. When studying from home, students do not have a teacher physically present to remind them to focus, complete their assignments, or stay alert during lessons. The sense of accountability that comes from being in a classroom tends to be missing. Group work is particularly valuable as it motivates students to learn from each other, encourages collaboration, and can make studying more enjoyable. However, when students are isolated, they may lose this motivation and fail to take their studies as seriously as they should.

In summary, learning through online classes at home is not a favorable approach for students. It deprives them of the comprehensive learning experience they get in school, limits their social and communication development, and can lead to a more careless attitude toward their education. For these reasons, attending school in person remains the better option for effective learning.

Some people believe that technology is merely an extension of our bodies. For instance, we carry our cell phones everywhere and rely on them constantly. While technology is a part of our daily lives, it can reduce face-to-face interaction and become a source of distraction. Although many argue that technology improves our lives, it often has harmful effects instead.

It is true that technology has some benefits. Since technology is integrated into our everyday routine, it assists us in numerous ways. For example, many jobs depend on technology, and using it makes work easier and more efficient. Communication is also improved through devices like cell phones, which help us stay in touch with others to check on their well-being or find their location in case of need. In education, tools such as computers and smartphones support students with their assignments and provide teachers with useful resources to enhance learning.

However, technology can be a major distraction. Cell phones, for example, are commonly used in schools, but they often divert students’ attention away from lessons and classmates. When students use their phones without permission, their grades tend to drop, and their interest in school diminishes. Moreover, cell phones can become addictive. Another example is texting or using a phone while driving, which distracts drivers and can lead to accidents. Even looking at GPS devices while behind the wheel takes attention away from the road. These examples show how distractions caused by technology can reduce focus and awareness of the environment.

Using cell phones can also decrease personal interaction. People often walk with their heads down, glued to their phones, especially teenagers and children. This behavior limits their communication with parents, friends, and family members. As a result, social skills suffer; many individuals no longer know how to start a conversation or greet others properly. This indicates that technology is harming our ability to connect with those around us, separating us from real-world experiences.

In conclusion, although some believe technology has positive effects, it frequently produces negative consequences. Technology is now an inseparable part of our lives, but it can cause distractions and reduce face-to-face communication. The problem lies not in technology itself, but in how we use it. If we limited our use of technology to necessary times only, the world would likely be a better place.

Online Learning

Who doesn't want to be left in the house all day using an electronic device with online access? Although students save money and time by taking classes from home. It is not beneficial to learn online because students lose focus of what they are learning and tend to easily get distracted when they're in their house, students can't have a one on one conversation with a teacher nor discuss with classmates, and students could also face technical difficulties when attending online classes from home.

Losing focus has a big impact in learning. For example, my friend Generic_Name sent me a text message last month, right when I started studying for my history mid-term exam. I responded back to Generic_Name's text, and without realizing we kept on messaging past midnight. This shows how easily students get distracted at home with a cellular device and how easy it is to lose focus. The next morning I decided to get to school an hour early and review one on one with my teacher.

Secondly, taking classes online doesn't just mean you don't have a physical teacher or instructor that you can question lively, but also means that it will be challenging to find answers to your questions. I remember in my sophomore year a kid in our econ class named Generic_Name was really sick for a while so he had ended up taking classes online. Generic_Name was a straight A student, always was first to answer the teachers questions and he also used to ask questions. Thankfully Generic_Name healed towards the end of the year and I asked him if he benefited and if he recommends attending classes from home. The straight A student Generic_Name said it was a real challenge to take the class online and he finished the class a month after he should have with a B- average. Generic_Name had also said that one of the most difficult parts about attending a class online was his laptop not functioning at all times, and not having a teacher you can talk and converse with one on one.

Finally, using your personal computer and internet connection can always be an issue. You can't always depend on your computer, not just the computers but even people aren't perfect. Another main problem Generic_Name had when attending classes online was his laptop and network connection. Generic_Name explained that he always faced technical difficulties. When his laptop wasn't functioning right, the only thing he could do was to stop the lesson and wait for his dad to get the laptop repaired, which took time. Each month, either his laptop or internet connection would not cooperate, so he finished the class a month later than everyone.

In conclusion, Everyone would like to save money and time by taking classes from home. But getting distracted, not asking your teacher questions when you need to, and wasting money on laptop repair is not worth it at all. Learning from a far distance could also be an option but when asking if it is beneficial, we can say that it is not by looking at the listed reasoning.

What about those times when you were sick at school, and no one could pick you up because you lived alone? Were your thoughts positive then, or were you just focused on getting through the day? A positive attitude alone does not guarantee success in school or in life. Everyone faces moments when they feel like giving up and escaping from all responsibilities.

After dedicating years to studying a career you didn’t enjoy, hoping it will lead to a good job and help support your family, you face many challenges. Long hours of part-time work, sleepless nights, countless essays and assignments, group projects, and sometimes not even being able to pay tuition—these are the realities university students encounter on their path to success, not merely a positive attitude. And once they finish, they must find a job and start repaying student loans. They have to prove in job interviews that they stand above all other candidates.

In conclusion, a successful life is achieved by reaching your goals, graduating from high school and university, and then finding a job that suits you. Not everyone can accomplish these steps because not everyone has the opportunity to attend high school or university. Many live each day hoping for a miracle, wishing they would win the lottery so they wouldn’t have to work anymore. But simply having a positive attitude will not take you anywhere; hard work is essential for true success.

Should schools regulate the number of extracurricular activities a student participates in? There should be some limits to how much control schools have over students' involvement in activities outside of class, but ultimately, it should be the student's family who makes those decisions. Schools should only step in if the student is failing classes, if the parents request a reduction, or if the student’s attendance at the activities is poor. In such cases, the school can assist in determining the best course of action.

To begin with, I believe there should be some boundaries regarding enrollment in extracurricular activities, but the decision should primarily rest with the student and their family because they know the student’s situation best. If the family feels that the student doesn’t have enough time for homework or studying, they should discuss this with the student and listen to their perspective. If the family agrees to let the student continue, that is their choice. However, if they decide that the student should reduce their commitments, they must inform the student's guidance counselor and the person in charge of the activity.

On the other hand, if a student’s grades start to fall or they begin failing classes, the guidance counselor should meet with the student to understand the cause. If it appears the student is overburdened with extracurriculars, a discussion should happen to decide which activities could be dropped temporarily to improve academic performance. This approach encourages students to maintain their grades if they wish to keep participating in their chosen activities.

Finally, if a student is frequently absent or inconsistent in attending meetings, they should not be allowed to continue in the extracurricular activity. Missing more than five meetings per month without a valid reason should lead to consequences, such as being removed from the club. Parents should be informed of the situation before the student is dismissed. With additional serious reasons, a temporary suspension from meetings could also be considered.

In summary, schools should have minimal influence over a student’s participation in extracurricular activities. The family ought to have the primary say, except in cases where the student’s academic performance is declining or their attendance in activities is poor. In such situations, schools can play a supportive role in guiding the student’s involvement.

Technology has both advantages and disadvantages—some aspects benefit humans, while others can be damaging and harmful. The question is whether technology has become essential in our daily lives or if it has made us too dependent on it, leading to laziness in doing things ourselves. I believe that reducing human interaction because of technology has brought many negative consequences, such as causing depression and isolation, making people lose their connection with reality, and damaging their physical or mental health. Therefore, technology can lead to several harmful effects.

To begin with, technology can lead to serious problems like depression and isolation, which can be very harmful, especially when they occur together. One reason depression results from technology is the widespread bullying that happens online, particularly on social media platforms, affecting many children globally and making them emotionally distressed. This often causes them to withdraw and avoid going to school. Moreover, many people spend a lot of time playing video games, sometimes to the extent that they isolate themselves from family and friends without realizing it. Given that almost everyone owns a smartphone or another device, many individuals remain glued to their screens all day and rarely go outside. This heavy use of technology can significantly affect people’s lives, contributing to feelings of depression.

In addition, technology can cause people to lose their grasp on reality. The internet allows misinformation and manipulation, which can easily influence others. Children, who enjoy watching TV and YouTube videos, often believe what they see because they are impressionable. Many online videos can mislead children or even influence how they think. Adults, too, can be affected, as conspiracy theories circulate claiming governments use technology to control minds—which some people believe. Others become so involved in video games that they start confusing the game world with real life, leading to harmful misunderstandings.

Furthermore, as technology advances, it can negatively impact our physical and mental health. Eye specialists warn that constantly staring at screens can harm our vision. Technology also shapes people’s behavior; some try to imitate internet personalities by changing their style or personality to fit online trends. In some cases, people watch videos of dangerous stunts and attempt to copy them, often resulting in serious injuries and hospital visits.

On the other hand, technology can be very helpful. It can save lives in emergencies and play an important role in defense during wars. It also makes many tasks more efficient and daily life easier, reducing stress that people used to face. Advances in technology have the potential to change the world for the better. However, technology is not perfect and can fail at critical moments, sometimes leading to fatal consequences. Although many believe technology will simplify life, relying too much on it may make life harder. If people depend entirely on machines, their physical fitness will decline because they are not exercising enough. Additionally, we need to recognize that technology contributes to environmental problems like pollution, which damages our planet.

In conclusion, technology is responsible for many serious problems today, even if we do not always notice them until we pause and reflect. I firmly believe that limiting face-to-face human contact because of technology can negatively affect people’s lives by causing depression, isolation, and a loss of connection with reality, as well as harming physical and mental well-being. Although technology can be ignored, it will never disappear from our lives.

The statement is "the first impression is almost impossible to change" which is a different feeling for everybody, but for me, I disagree. In fact, the first impression is really important and sometimes true, but I think the first impression does not define a person, an object or a situation. Having a first impression is a human reflex, like having an opinion or a judgment. We are doing it unconsciously.

The first impression is most of the time not real, you need to search deeper to make an opinion and when you really have an opinion, then, the first impression is not important anymore. For example, when you meet someone, your first impression might be that you think she is supercilious and even a little bit mean. Therefore when you really get to know her deeper then you will find that she just had a bad day and that she is nice and sociable. Sometimes it's the contrary, a person seems really nice but in reality she is not, so your first impression was wrong. It is not good to stay on a first impression because most of the time it's wrong.

Moreover, the physic, behaviors or attitude can change an impression. If the person do not smile and seems to be rude but in reality is the nicest person, then it will be awkward for you because you thought she was bad. Sometimes a person can have a bad reputation because of the first impression he shows and it is not his fault, some persons just don't smile every time. Sometimes you can be disappointed because you didn't get to know the person because of your first impression.

The first impressions is not only for people but also for a situation or an object. For example if you are in a library and you want to buy a book, the first thing you are going to do is looking at the cover of the book. If it's pretty you will more easily choose this one instead of a book with a black cover and only the title, because it is your first impression. But your first impression is wrong because you didn't take time to read the resume and you will find soon that the pretty book is actually boring instead of the black book which is really interesting. An object can look nice but have a bad quality. The first impression is the color and the shape of the object, like the physic and the attitude of a person.

In conclusion I would say that the first impression is sometimes right but most of the time it's not. In my opinion, you must not keep in mind your first impression of a person, it's most of the time wrong. You have to get to know the person to build your own opinion. It is normal to have a first impression, like judging, but you must not take the habit to stick with your first impression.

The phrase "the first impression is almost impossible to change" means different things to different people, but personally, I disagree with it. While a first impression can be significant and sometimes accurate, I believe it does not fully represent a person, object, or situation. Forming a first impression is a natural human reaction, similar to having an opinion or making a quick judgment, and it often happens without conscious thought.

Usually, first impressions are not entirely accurate. To form a true opinion, you need to look beyond the surface. Once you have a more informed view, the initial impression becomes less important. For instance, if you meet someone and at first you think they seem arrogant or unfriendly, getting to know them better might reveal that they were just having a bad day and are actually kind and sociable. Sometimes the opposite occurs: someone who appears warm and friendly at first might not be like that underneath, showing that your first impression was mistaken. Because of this, relying solely on first impressions can be misleading.

Additionally, a person's appearance, behavior, or attitude can affect how we perceive them initially. If someone looks serious and does not smile, but is actually very kind, it can create an awkward situation because you judged them wrongly at first. Sometimes people develop bad reputations simply due to their first impression, which may not be fair since some individuals do not smile often. As a result, people may miss the chance to get to know someone better, leading to disappointment based on that initial judgment.

First impressions are not only relevant to people but also to situations or objects. For example, when choosing a book in a library, the first thing that catches your attention might be its cover. You may be more drawn to a colorful, attractive cover rather than a plain one, forming a positive impression of the book. However, this impression can be incorrect because the interesting story might be inside the plain book, while the pretty cover could hide a boring content. Similarly, an object’s appearance, like its color and shape, can be compared to a person’s looks and behavior—both can be deceiving in judging quality or character.

In conclusion, I believe that although first impressions can occasionally be correct, they are often misleading. It is important not to hold onto your initial opinion of a person because it is frequently wrong. Instead, you should take the time to really get to know someone before forming a final judgment. Having first impressions is natural, but it is best not to make the mistake of sticking to them without further understanding.

Don't judge a book by its cover

Many people believe that distance learning is an excellent choice for students. It offers several advantages, including improved attendance, fewer issues, and important support for students with disabilities or health challenges. However, there are those who argue that not attending traditional school in person can lead to students becoming lazy and irresponsible. Despite this, distance learning presents clear benefits for both students and educational institutions.

One of the main advantages of distance learning is better attendance. When students have the option to attend classes from home, they are less likely to miss school. A common frustration for many students is having to wake up early in the morning to get ready and spend long hours at school. This early routine and lengthy day can often lead to tiredness and a lack of motivation.

Some students are unable to physically attend school due to certain disabilities or medical conditions. These students still deserve an education, and distance learning provides an effective way for them to participate in classes from home. Among the many benefits of distance education, giving students with disabilities the chance to learn is one of the most important.

Another benefit is the reduction of problems that can occur in a school environment. Many students face bullying or are involved in unnecessary drama while at school. Learning from home helps eliminate these social difficulties since students do not have to interact directly with peers who may cause trouble. This can result in a safer, more focused learning experience and fewer bullying incidents.

On the other hand, critics believe that studying at home might make students careless and unmotivated. Nevertheless, students should have the freedom to choose how they want to learn. If a student becomes lazy due to distance learning, the issue lies with the student’s own attitude, not the learning method. In fact, many would argue that distance education can encourage students to be more disciplined and responsible.

In conclusion, distance learning offers significant benefits such as improved attendance, support for students with disabilities, and fewer social problems at school. While some worry about the potential negative effects on students’ motivation, the overall advantages make distance learning a valuable option for many learners.

When students decide on a specific goal, they often feel stuck, worrying that if they don’t succeed quickly, they will fall behind. This kind of pressure can make it difficult to concentrate on other subjects because their attention becomes too narrowly focused. High school is a period of personal growth and change, and students may discover new interests along the way. Therefore, it’s better not to put yourself in a position that causes unnecessary stress.

Pressure is a common part of life today, but it is far from enjoyable. Feeling pressured to succeed is one of the hardest experiences because it creates an overwhelming need to make others proud—whether parents, teachers, or school administrators. In the case of choosing a career early, students often try to prove their commitment to those around them. However, as the pressure builds over time, it can lead to feelings of sadness, depression, and losing touch with one’s true self since the motivation is based on others’ expectations rather than personal desires.

High school changes people’s perspectives in many ways. When you first enter high school, it’s not like the movies often show; it’s a place where both students and teachers focus on their own work and growth. Compared to middle school, high school offers much tougher classes and a wide variety of electives to explore. This variety encourages students to discover new interests, which might change their future plans. Because of this, it makes little sense to decide on a career path early when you haven’t had the chance to try different subjects and see what you truly enjoy.

From my own experience and what I have heard from others, I believe it is better not to commit to a career at a young age. In high school, try different classes that interest you and continue with the ones you enjoy. If you don’t like a subject, don’t be afraid to switch to something else. Life is different from what you often see on TV, so it’s important to explore and learn before making a final decision.

Everyone is unique, and you are no exception. A career is just a word right now—there’s no need to pressure yourself into choosing one too early. Give yourself time to grow and discover what truly suits you.

Education plays a crucial role in preparing individuals for the challenges of an ever-changing world. It influences how future workers respond to various situations and solve problems. Entire generations have been shaped by the knowledge they gained in school, from basic skills like math and language to advancements that have allowed humanity to reach the Moon and address global issues. This foundation has helped shape the world as we know it today. I believe that extending the school day is not a good idea for several reasons: the current timetable already provides enough time for both mental and physical growth, adding more hours could lead to increased unproductive and negative experiences for students, and it might cause scheduling conflicts for students, parents, and staff.

Firstly, the existing seven-hour school day can already be quite demanding. Students often arrive with challenges, such as rushing to catch the bus or dealing with the stress of being late. Throughout the day, they are expected to grasp complex ideas, complete assignments, and manage their belongings, like lockers. They may also worry about social situations or upcoming deadlines. In short, students’ daily routines can be filled with stressful and difficult moments, making their time at school quite intense even now.

If the school day were to be extended, these everyday struggles might worsen, and new problems could emerge. For instance, students might face an increased workload, more homework, and longer periods that could become tedious after a while. Some classes may need to be shortened to fit the extended schedule, possibly reducing the quality of learning. The added hours could result in students feeling overwhelmed and unable to keep up with their responsibilities, which can be discouraging for many.

Another important point is that a longer school day could lead to conflicts between the schedules of students, parents, and teachers. Many students participate in extracurricular activities, such as sports teams, that require sufficient time to practice and compete. Parents might find it hard to adjust their own work routines to accommodate later school hours, which could create additional stress at home. Teachers might also have to stay late to finish grading or prepare lessons, increasing their workload. This imbalance in schedules could negatively impact the entire school community.

While there are some benefits to extending school hours—such as more time for in-depth study, completing homework during school, and longer opportunities for socializing during breaks—these advantages do not outweigh the potential downsides. Even with these benefits, unproductive situations and challenges may still persist.

In conclusion, I am against extending the school day because it would cause scheduling conflicts for many people, increase negative experiences for students, and disrupt a schedule that already involves numerous activities and responsibilities. Parents and guardians may struggle to adjust their work commitments, homework demands could rise, and students and teachers alike may experience increased stress. Although there are some positives to a longer school day, the possible consequences should be carefully considered, as these changes could have lasting impacts.

I am not against teachers helping students, but I believe they should focus on supporting those who genuinely try. Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

They need this time to relax their minds and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain is mostly focused on schoolwork. I admit that at multiple points during the year my brain feels worn down and damaged from being in this state constantly. It does not get a chance to heal until the summer, when school is over. If we were to have a year-round school year, this mental fatigue would persist year-round as well. In that case, a student's brain would eventually break down and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year-round school schedule.

Although the strongest argument for a year-round school year is that students cannot retain enough information for the next school year, I believe I have a stronger counterclaim and solution to this problem. A simple way to address the issue of retaining information is to make mandatory—but simple—assignments from the previous year for students to complete over the summer. This way, students can enjoy their long summer break to refresh their brains and do their activities without forgetting important information. You get the best of both worlds, with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion, I think my reasons for keeping summer break the way it is are much stronger than the arguments for a year-round school year. Implementing a year-round school schedule would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous, as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone once said, "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

Many students look forward to summer vacation, yet some educators argue that this break is excessively long and that students tend to forget what they have learned, making it harder to retain knowledge by the time school resumes in the fall. Because of this, some suggest implementing a year-round school calendar with shorter summer holidays of about three to four weeks and longer breaks spaced throughout the year. However, I disagree with this idea and believe that summer vacation should remain as it is.

One reason I oppose year-round schooling is that it would disrupt many summer activities and even affect some students’ work plans. For example, summer is a popular time for students to engage in sports, travel, or other hobbies without the pressure of schoolwork. They prefer to enjoy these activities during a lengthy break because it allows them to focus entirely on what they love without worrying about studying. Similarly, summer jobs or internships are important opportunities for students to learn financial responsibility by earning and saving money. Additionally, those interested in specific careers can gain valuable experience through internships. Introducing a year-round schedule would make it difficult or unappealing for students to participate in these activities during the breaks.

Another, and perhaps more crucial, reason relates to students’ mental health. According to an article by Complex News about youth well-being, over 40% of students feel depressed or mentally exhausted by the end of their freshman year in high school. This percentage grows even higher as students advance through school. The summer break serves as a vital period for students to rest and recharge after nearly ten months of continuous learning. Speaking from personal experience, throughout the school year, my brain often feels overwhelmed and drained due to constant focus on academic work. It is only during the summer that I can truly relax and recover mentally. If schools adopted a year-round schedule, students’ brains would remain under constant strain with little chance to recover, which could lead to burnout or serious mental health issues. No student should have to face such consequences because of an extended school calendar.

While it is true that one of the main arguments for year-round schooling is to improve retention of knowledge between school years, I believe there is a better way to address this issue. A simple solution could be assigning light, mandatory review work from the previous year during the summer. This would help students keep important information fresh in their minds without sacrificing the length of their summer vacation. This approach offers the benefits of both worlds—students can enjoy a long break to rejuvenate, while still maintaining their academic progress—without the need to implement a year-round schedule.

In summary, I believe the reasons supporting a traditional summer break are much stronger than those favoring year-round schooling. Changing to a year-round system would unnecessarily complicate students’ summer plans and pose risks to their mental health. As the saying goes, “If it isn’t broken, don’t fix it.”

In my view, I generally disagree with schools offering distance learning as an option for students to attend classes from home through online platforms or video conferencing. This is not because I attend a public high school, but because I believe there are important reasons against it.

One major reason for my disagreement is that online classes can negatively impact students' communication skills. When you attend classes from home, you are not physically surrounded by your classmates, so you mainly interact with your teacher only. Although I have never experienced an online class myself, I believe it is important for students to engage with their peers. Working with other students can help you understand things better, especially when you encounter difficulties. Without face-to-face interaction, it is harder to receive assistance from fellow classmates, which may limit learning opportunities.

Another reason why I am against distance learning is that it reduces participation skills. In school, we often take part in activities related to the subjects we study, which greatly helps us remember the material. It is also easier to ask questions and clarify doubts in person. If you don’t understand something during a face-to-face lesson, you can immediately discuss it with the teacher. In contrast, asking questions through emails or messages might lead to delays in responses, which could affect your grades. Therefore, direct interaction with teachers seems much more effective for learning.

Lastly, completing classes from home could cause students to become lazy or skip sessions. This can harm their academic performance, especially if they are not disciplined. For instance, I know that distance learning would not suit me personally because I tend to procrastinate, and I might miss lessons due to oversleeping or other reasons. However, some students are organized and responsible enough to manage online education successfully. For those individuals, distance learning could be a good choice as they are committed to completing their studies carefully.

In conclusion, although it is positive that schools provide distance learning as an alternative for students with valid reasons for not attending in person, I do not agree with it generally. The impact on communication, participation, and motivation makes me believe that face-to-face schooling is better for most students.

In conclusion, schools have to offer distance learning as an option for students to attend classes from home.

This essay will explore the challenges and benefits associated with working in groups compared to working alone, focusing on the impact on the individual rather than the group as a whole. To begin, we will examine the differences between group work and individual effort, then consider the various factors involved when working as part of a team. Finally, we will analyze how these factors can either support or hinder a person's performance.

Think back to a time when you had to complete a project. You probably considered different approaches, and one of the first decisions was whether to work individually or as part of a group. Most people understand what it means to work alone since they are solely responsible for the task. However, it is important to clarify what exactly a group is, how it is formed, and the dynamics that come into play during group work.

A group can be defined as several individuals who come together to achieve a specific goal or complete a particular task. The way a group is structured, how it operates, and the processes it follows are all part of what is known as group dynamics. These dynamics apply to both formal and informal groups across various settings. In organizations especially, groups are a common feature, making the study of group dynamics a key topic within organizational behavior.

Group dynamics primarily focus on understanding why groups form, how they develop, and how they function. Many theories have been put forward to explain these processes.

While working in a group has many advantages, it also presents certain disadvantages. For example, individual members often have less control over the task compared to working alone. Some group members may dominate the project, while others may contribute very little. Although the group as a whole might reach its objectives, this imbalance can limit the involvement and growth of some individuals. On the other hand, a well-functioning group can accomplish more than individuals working separately because it brings together a wider variety of skills. Moreover, sharing and discussing ideas in a group can greatly enhance your understanding of the subject.

Being part of a team also helps you develop important interpersonal skills such as effective communication and active listening. It fosters teamwork abilities, including leadership and motivating others, which are valuable not only during your studies but also in many other aspects of life.

To fully benefit from group work, it is essential to manage it efficiently. This involves ensuring that everyone participates and the group’s goals are met without compromising individual learning and contribution.

This is why I say that if we value self-reliance, we need help from experts; that way, we can succeed in life. However, there are some decisions that we can take by ourselves. For example, we can choose whether we want to drink alcohol or smoke. For that type of decision, we just have to think about who we are hurting too, and as we know, it is ourselves and nobody else. If we don't think about ourselves and the decisions that we make, nobody will.

Reason 1

In my opinion, self-reliance is really important in every single person’s life. When we talk about self-reliance, it is about decisions. There are times when we think we are right in every decision we make. However, we have to know that no one is perfect as a human. So, there are times when we make bad choices. One good example could be when we are teenagers. At that age, we need more help than anything because there are a lot of things that can influence us really easily. At that time, we need help from experts, and what better experts than our parents? They want the best for us, so they will teach us what could be the best and what really matters in this life because they love us. I'm not talking in general because there are some parents that don't really care about what their son or daughter is doing, but some of them do. Also, we can look for other types of experts who can be professional and have a diploma in what they are experts in. So, it can be really helpful for us to succeed because they have been studying their career for years. Also, it can help us to make better decisions throughout life and make us better people.

Reason 2

Bad decisions can hurt ourselves. Decision-making is something that we all have to do one day. It could be a good or bad decision, or sometimes there are decisions that look good but could lead us to do something bad. However, there are decisions that can hurt ourselves and take us to do something stupid in life. For example, a person wants to invest money to create a restaurant. At first, it sounds good because what we all think is that we only win in this type of business, but the reality is that it could be a challenge for the person. Some people don’t take time to think about the consequences of creating a restaurant. They don’t think about the things they have to pay out from the money they are making from the restaurant. They don’t think about the fact that they can lose all their money if the restaurant doesn’t work. When this happens and people lose all their money, they can get depressed, and some have even taken their lives. So, here is when we need help from experts and not make the decision to create the restaurant by ourselves. Those people that we call experts know a lot more than us because they have graduated in it. They know everything about business and what could be best for us. So, we can succeed in business life and not lose money.

Counterclaim

Someone would argue that making decisions by ourselves is better because that way we won't have to blame anybody if we make a bad decision. Also, we can learn how to be responsible for the decisions that we make. However, we don’t need to wait until that happens; it is better to look for experts so they can help us make good decisions and not bad decisions. Two heads are better than one.

Conclusion

In conclusion, help from experts is the best way to do things. They can teach us how to be better, and that’s why they have been created in this world—to look for them and ask for help. Sometimes we need to accept that we can't do it by ourselves and that we need help from experts or our parents. We have to look for different sources to succeed in life. At some points, we have to be strong, but to make any decision, we need to be social. What I mean by this is to ask for help and make good decisions.

People who value self-reliance should turn to experts and authorities for advice rather than making important life decisions entirely on their own. Experts are individuals with much deeper knowledge on certain subjects compared to us. A simple way to understand this is by thinking about the relationship between teachers and students. Teachers have completed extensive training in their field, for example, science. They have to work hard to gain their expertise. This is why I believe that even if we appreciate self-reliance, seeking guidance from experts is necessary to achieve success in life. Of course, there are some choices we can make independently, such as deciding whether to drink alcohol or smoke. For these kinds of personal decisions, we need to consider who might be affected, and often the only person hurt is ourselves. If we do not take care of ourselves and think carefully about the choices we make, nobody else will do it for us.

I believe self-reliance plays a crucial role in everyone’s life, especially when it comes to making decisions. Sometimes we may be confident that the choices we make are right, but nobody is perfect, and mistakes happen. A good example is during the teenage years, when people are easily influenced by many things. At this stage, we need more support than ever, and who better to help than experts—like our parents? Most parents want the best for their children, and they try to guide them toward what truly matters in life because they care deeply. Of course, not all parents are supportive, but many are. In addition to parents, we can also consult other professionals who have specialized education and diplomas in their fields. These experts can be very helpful in guiding us toward better decisions and personal growth.

Poor decisions can cause serious harm to ourselves. Everyone faces choices, some good and some bad, and sometimes decisions that seem positive at first can lead to negative outcomes. For example, consider someone who wants to invest money in opening a restaurant. At first, this might seem like a great plan because many believe the business will be successful. However, in reality, running a restaurant is challenging, and some people don’t think carefully about the potential risks, such as the expenses they must cover or the possibility of losing all their investment. When this happens, the person can become depressed, and in extreme cases, some may even take their own lives. This is where guidance from experts is invaluable. Business professionals who have studied the field extensively understand the risks and know what steps to take to increase the chances of success. By consulting them, people can avoid losing money and make wiser choices.

Some may argue that making decisions on our own is better because it means we won’t blame others if things go wrong, and it teaches us responsibility. However, instead of waiting for mistakes to happen, it is wiser to seek advice from experts beforehand. Two heads are often better than one, and getting support can help us avoid poor decisions.

In conclusion, seeking help from experts is the best approach to handling important matters. They can guide us toward improvement and success, which is why they exist—to be a resource when we need assistance. Sometimes we must acknowledge that we cannot do everything alone and should seek help from parents or trained professionals. To succeed in life, it is important not only to be strong but also to be social in the sense of asking for advice and making informed decisions.

Many students finish high school early to start college sooner. In fact, I believe that graduating in three years and spending time working before college is a better choice. This approach helps students save money for college, become more mature, and develop strong time management skills. These benefits provide valuable opportunities before continuing their higher education.
