Often, students need to take out loans because they cannot afford tuition, and their parents may not be able to help financially. Loans, however, create debt that has to be repaid later. If students finish school in three years and then work, they can save up for college themselves. This way, they may avoid loans, reducing financial stress for both students and their families. Taking responsibility for their own finances also shows maturity and independence, which can make their parents proud.

Secondly, working before attending college helps students become more mature. Graduating early often means students are only 17 years old, which can be challenging socially and academically. Spending a year working helps them gain experience, become responsible, and better understand the world beyond school. Maturity is important because it teaches students to meet deadlines and behave professionally, skills needed in college. Moreover, since some younger students may face bullying or feel isolated, working a year allows them to join college alongside peers their age, creating a smoother transition and a better social environment.

Lastly, having a job develops essential time management skills. Many students struggle to submit assignments on time, but work demands punctuality and meeting deadlines. These habits transfer well to college life where managing time is key to success. Good time management means planning enough hours for studying, classes, sleep, and relaxation. Learning to organize daily activities helps students avoid lateness and missed work, making their college experience less stressful and more productive.

Some people might argue that students should go straight to college after high school, but I respectfully disagree. If students start college without enough maturity, they may find the adjustment difficult and struggle academically and socially. Taking time to work beforehand offers valuable life lessons and prepares them better for college challenges.

In summary, I believe that students who choose to work before starting college gain important advantages. They save money, build maturity through responsibility, and improve their time management skills. These benefits help them enter college more prepared and confident, leading to greater success in their education and future.

Connecting with others can provide valuable support and guidance that can improve our performance and open new opportunities.

Scientist Albert Einstein once said, "Imagination is more important than knowledge." Now imagine yourself as a beginning engineer, sitting at your desk, aggravated because you can't come up with a new invention. All you have around you are textbooks but no image or thought of what your invention may be. If only you could imagine a new invention of some sort then maybe you could build something. But with no imagination, how can you build knowledge? I agree with Einstein's quote. I believe imagination is more important than knowledge.

I agree with Einstein's quote because having imagination is how we've had all our inventions yet. Without imagination how were many of the things we own invented? For example, the telephone. The telephone couldn't have been invented without someone imagining a device where you could communicate without leaving your home. You need imagination in order to make new things. Another example would be the camera. Whoever invented it, had to have imagination in order to think of a device that captures any moment almost in an instant. Even I, as a student, need imagination in order to make new things. For example, when making an essay, such as this one, I need to imagine of a good story hook that goes along with the prompt.

Furthermore, I believe in Einstein quote because without imagination, knowledge is almost useless. For example, when learning a new vocabulary list. You may know all the definitions but you can't put them in your own words or use the words in different instances. Why? Because you can't imagine it. You can't picture it, you just know the definitions. Another example is when reading a book. Knowing how to read isn't even near of what you need to fully comprehend a book. You need to imagine it. Picture the story in your mind in order to fully understand the book's theme, setting and tone.

Lastly, I agree in Einstein's quote because without imagination, all our decisions would be made carelessly. For instance, before you speak or move, most of the time you imagine what the outcome of that action will be. If not, the outcome won't be for the better. Another instance is when in an experiment, you hypothesize what the result of the experiment will be. That takes imagination. When signing a contract, it's needed to imagine the consequences of signing and not signing the contract. In other words, you need to imagine things before you decide to take them on. Knowledge isn't the only thing that will help you when making decisions.

In conclusion, Einstein's quote is correct in my perspective. Knowledge isn't the most important factor to have, imagination is key to everything you do and will do. You can't fully understand most things without imagining them. Can't go on inventing things before imagining them first. Also, you won't be able to make good decisions before imagining the outcome. All in all, imagination is also how you'll enjoy your life. Knowledge is great and all but it can't bring others as much happiness as imagination can. It's how we've been happy for all these years. Imagination is how we have gone so far in this world and how much we've survived.

Are vacations a necessity to us and to our success? Why do we need them? While some say that inactivity gives us time to reinvent ourselves. Others believe that it instigates procrastination. Inactivity serves a purpose because it keeps us from giving up and it allows us time for new ideas.

Inactivity serves a purpose because it keeps us from giving up. For example, I was once taking a very long test that lasted around 4 to 5 hours. At first, I was just guessing my way through it because I was very tired and ready to give up. Then, we were given a five minute break so I got up and walked around a bit. After walking for a few minutes, I was energized and ready to finish the test. With my new found energy, I was very content with the test and my score. In fact, students who take mental breaks during long testing periods score 31% higher than the ones who did not take any breaks. In conclusion, inactivity keeps us enthusiastic about our work.

Inactivity serves a purpose because it allows us time for new ideas. For example, one of my friends named Generic_Name once did not go to school for three days. During these three days, she organized her school essentials and cleaned up her room. Since she was working on a project before the break, she had time to finish it and she even had another project idea for her science class. She obtained a good grade on both projects. In fact, students who have taken breaks during long tests, like the SOL, say that after their break they had a better understanding of the test. Even the workforce workers are encouraged to take a few days off. It helps the worker get more creative. Even the owner of a business need a vacation. In fact, around 56% of entrepreneurs say that they came up with at least one new idea after a vacation. Inactivity helps prepare our minds for when we are active.

Have you ever had a really important decision you had to make? Did you feel overwhelmed because you didn't know what you should do? Asking for help or advise from people such as friends and family around you can really help alleviate all that stress. Most people encounter big decisions often throughout their lives, so getting advise from numerous people can help you get more input on something, and may end up helping you make a final decision. Seeking multiple opinions can really help someone make a better choice when dealing with decision making.

One way seeking multiple opinions can help someone make a better choice is that by asking more than one person, they can get more input. Asking numerous people can be a huge help when making an important decision. Not only are people getting different ideas of what they may want to do, they can also get advise from people who may be more experienced than themselves. For example, if someone was debating on which college they should apply to, they may end up asking people such as older siblings or parents for advise because they may have more experience with that matter. By asking multiple people, you can get multiple ideas, each of them being different in their own way. By getting more people's input, you may be able to start to make your own choice about the matter because of the advise you've gotten.

Another way seeking multiple opinions can help someone make a better choice is by not getting any biased opinions. By asking more than one person for advise on a subject, they can get more than one new idea that isn't one of their own. This way, they can get more than one person's thoughts on the decision, and have different ideas on it. For example, if someone were trying to make a decision on what sport they may want to tryout for at school, they could possibly ask their friends and family about which they should choose. However, they should also ask people like classmates and teachers, as they may have their own ideas, and won't give the person any biased ideas or information. Friends and family can have a great deal of influence on people, so it's important to always get people's thoughts that are on the outside. This will make it to where there's a greater chance of the decision maker not being biased, as they've heard numerous people's thoughts, and can make their own decision off of that.

A final way seeking multiple opinions can help someone make a better choice is by being more prepared about the choice they're going to make. The decision maker can use all the advise they've gotten from different people to make their own choice, and feel better prepared. They will be more focused as they know what they want to do, and will feel more confident and less overwhelmed. Feeling less overwhelmed can be a big help as the person doesn't have to be so worried, so they won't have any distractions from making the best possible decision. For example, if someone is trying to decide what kind of car they want to get, and they've gotten advise from numerous people, they can make a better choice when picking. They'll know exactly what they want, as they've heard many thoughts from the people around them, and so they can make their final decision.

After getting advise from multiple people around them, the decision maker may be able to make the best choice possible, as they've gotten new thoughts and ideas. Asking for help or for some advise from those around you can help you make the best possible choice because you've gotten a lot of new information and opinions that you wouldn't have gotten if you had only asked one or no one at all for advise. Making an important choice can seem a little bit easier and less stressful after seeking advise from multiple people. Getting help from others around you can help you make the best choice you can.

When asking just one person, their views might influence the decision too much, especially if they have a personal connection. But by talking to various individuals—including friends, family, classmates, and teachers—a person can hear different thoughts and reduce the risk of bias. For instance, when deciding which sport to try out for at school, it can be helpful to get opinions not only from close friends but also from others who might offer an impartial perspective. Since friends and family might unintentionally sway someone’s thinking, getting outside viewpoints ensures a more balanced understanding, helping the decision-maker follow their own judgment.

Lastly, seeking advice from many sources can help someone feel more prepared and confident about their choice. Gathering different pieces of advice can clear confusion and make the decision-maker more certain about their next steps. This increased clarity reduces feelings of stress and distraction. For example, if a person is choosing a car and has talked to numerous people, they will likely be more focused and confident when making the final decision. Knowing they have considered many viewpoints allows them to feel ready and less overwhelmed.

In conclusion, getting advice from multiple people can help someone make the best possible decision by providing fresh ideas and reducing bias. Asking for help from those around you introduces valuable information that you might have missed if you only consulted one person or no one at all. Making tough choices can become easier and less stressful by hearing different opinions, and this support can lead to wiser decisions. Seeking advice from others is a helpful way to find the best solution.

To begin this discussion, I want to raise an important question that many people rarely consider: "How does technology affect our health?" This is a crucial issue that deserves thoughtful attention.

Technology has become deeply embedded in our daily routines. From the moment we wake up until we go to sleep, we interact with numerous devices, software applications, and tools. Technology enables us to accomplish a wide range of activities without any face-to-face interaction. For example, people can borrow books, shop, or play games all without talking to another person. Unfortunately, this reduction in human contact due to technology has had detrimental effects on people's well-being.

Some might argue that limiting human interaction through technology has positive benefits, but the majority agree that this lack of real-life connection has harmful consequences.

If we compare two individuals, one who relies heavily on technology for everything—shopping, reading, gaming, doing schoolwork, and even communicating with friends and family—and another who prefers to avoid technology, choosing instead to visit stores, meet loved ones in person, and engage in more physical activities, the first person is more likely to experience health problems. These problems may include sickness, pain, or even depression earlier than the second person. This is because excessive use of computers and devices encourages a sedentary lifestyle and often results in poor posture, neck strain, back problems, and hearing difficulties. Such issues can develop into chronic pain and discomfort that are difficult to treat.

Now that we have explored this topic more thoroughly, let's revisit the question posed earlier: "How does technology affect our health?" If we genuinely considered this question, we would recognize that technology does not positively impact our health. Instead, it contributes to stress, vision problems, back pain, hearing loss, and other negative outcomes. Additionally, heavy technology use can lead to feelings of isolation and depression because people lack meaningful social interaction. Psychological research shows that everyone needs at least one close friend to talk to during tough times. This need is not met when people spend most of their time alone using devices, which explains why frequent technology users can feel lonely and avoid engaging with those around them.

In summary, technology allows people to accomplish many tasks without direct social contact, but this reduction in human interaction has negatively affected people's lives. If individuals do not learn to manage their time and avoid overusing technology, future generations will face the same challenges we do now. The unfortunate reality is that since technological advancement is deeply ingrained in society, reversing this trend seems unlikely. What are the benefits of working with a group and working alone? I believe that working in groups helps you to have more ideas, more knowledge, because if you communicate with your group members, they'll think about different ideas to proceed the work that is getting done. Working alone sometimes helps you more than working with groups because you are responsible for your own work.

I rather work by myself because I've had bad experience working with groups. When I work in groups sometimes I'm the one that has to do all the work, and in my opinion if we are working in groups we have to help each other, communicate and share our thoughts because if we don't do that what's the point of working in groups. The type of impression formed depends heavily on how the brain processes and responds to the circumstances. Additionally, when people move to a new country like the United States, their minds go through a significant adjustment, creating many new impressions as they adapt to a different way of life. The brain’s role is essential in making these first impressions and helping people adjust.

In summary, first impressions are very difficult to change because they arise naturally and instantly as a result of encountering something new. As people explore new experiences, these initial reactions happen automatically and shape their perceptions.

Technology has become so advanced that it allows students and teachers to conduct and attend classes online. Many students today face the question: what are the advantages and disadvantages of online learning? This is an important consideration for those trying to decide whether to take online courses. Since many students balance part-time or full-time jobs alongside their education, their time is extremely valuable. To make an informed choice, they need to understand the pros and cons of online classes. I believe online learning offers a great opportunity because it provides flexibility, a wide range of courses, easy access to instructors, and often accelerated programs.

First of all, one of the biggest advantages of online classes is their flexibility. Students can usually complete coursework at any time during the day or week that suits them. Although there are assignments to write and research to conduct, the timing is often up to the student's convenience. This flexibility is especially beneficial for students who work, as they can fit the classes around their work schedules. Many people work afternoons or evenings, so attending traditional in-person classes can be impossible for them. Online courses make it easier to manage both work and study responsibilities.

Another strong benefit is the availability of almost any subject through online programs. Distance learning options are offered by many colleges, and it is simple to find courses by searching online. Contrary to the common belief that online students lack contact with their teachers, many virtual courses actually provide better access to faculty. Shy students, in particular, may feel more comfortable asking questions online and can often receive answers quickly, which enhances their learning experience.

Finally, online classes offer convenience for both undergraduate and graduate students who can study and complete their work according to their own schedules. This flexibility is crucial for those juggling work and family commitments. Additionally, many students want to take accelerated courses to finish their studies sooner. Online classes are well suited for this because traditional classroom settings often move at the pace of the slowest student, resulting in delays. Online programs allow learners to progress faster if they are ready, which saves time and keeps motivated students engaged.

In conclusion, online learning lets students study at their own speed, as long as they meet deadlines and participate appropriately. However, it also demands strong self-discipline and time management skills since students work independently without immediate supervision. Beyond teaching subjects like geology or poetry, online education helps students develop self-motivation, an important quality that can distinguish them in their careers and personal lives. It encourages learners to make thoughtful decisions and maintain an open mind, preparing them to succeed far beyond the classroom.

Technology is often hailed as one of the greatest achievements of the 21st century, and it is hard to find someone who doesn’t appreciate its benefits. But is technology really as wonderful as it seems? When I was younger, people would warn that technology might harm our social lives. At the time, I didn’t believe them, but now I understand their concerns.

The main purpose of technology is to simplify tasks, not to isolate us or cause health problems. I believe technology holds incredible potential, but we are not using it wisely. Instead of helping us lead healthier lives, it often encourages unhealthy habits. For example, rather than cooking our own meals, many of us order food that is far less nutritious. Another significant issue is how dependent people have become on technology; some feel as if they couldn’t live without it. The widespread use of social media, in particular, has replaced many face-to-face conversations and is a major reason why people choose virtual communication over personal interaction.

On the other hand, technology has its positive sides as well as its drawbacks. One of its greatest advantages is saving time in everyday activities. In the past, people had to rely on postal mail, which took days or even weeks to deliver messages. Now, thanks to modern technology, communication can happen within minutes. Additionally, technology enables us to reduce environmental damage by creating energy-efficient homes, cars, and airplanes that run on electricity instead of fossil fuels. Renewable energy sources like solar panels, wind turbines, and hydroelectric power provide nearly unlimited electricity, as long as natural disasters do not disrupt these resources. For the foreseeable future, these energy sources offer a clean alternative to polluting fuels.

Furthermore, I consider technology an incredible invention for humanity. Although it can have negative effects, the solutions are quite simple. If we avoid letting social media and technology control our lives and treat them as tools rather than essentials, many problems can be prevented. Technology has evolved dramatically from its early days when it was used just to light a bulb. Today, it powers nearly everything we rely on—from cars and homes to entire cities.

Lastly, despite all these amazing advancements, technology has also distracted us and led to social isolation. While it is undoubtedly a remarkable innovation, it can be damaging to our social relationships. Humans are naturally social beings, and anything that diminishes our ability to connect with each other will lead to negative consequences. Our species has developed social skills over thousands of years, and now we are risking undoing that progress. In conclusion, technology is a valuable part of our lives, but it does not contribute positively to our social well-being.

Can a person continue to grow if they only focus on mastering one skill and never attempt anything new? Some believe that being satisfied with what they have already achieved is enough. It is true that one can become highly skilled in a particular field, but if they never explore beyond that area, their development will be limited. Choosing to specialize in one thing is fine, but in that case, their knowledge will only expand within that specific domain and not beyond. People cannot truly progress if they remain fixed on what they have already mastered and refuse to learn new things.

Growth becomes difficult when someone sticks exclusively to their area of expertise. Take, for instance, Ms. Generic_Name, an attractive woman who owns a plant shop and teaches others about plants. She once explained to some children that plants do not grow on their own; people have to help them grow. She took the children to the back of the store to show them an apple seed. Ms. Generic_Name admitted that she used to care for the plants carefully but stopped because she assumed that once they had grown, her job was done. She saw the plant standing tall and thought no further effort was needed. However, she did not realize that without continued care, the plants would stop growing. This is similar to people who master something but then do not try anything else—they become stagnant and unable to grow any further. Therefore, if someone feels comfortable with just what they have learned and does not attempt anything new, they will not experience growth.

Acquiring knowledge is a key factor in personal growth. For example, Ms. Generic_Name once had only a basic understanding of plants. At first, she was unaware of the care needed for them until they became strong enough. Over time, as she gained experience, her knowledge expanded significantly. She refused to remain limited to what she already knew and continued to grow intellectually. She is now attending college, studying various types of plants from different countries. Thanks to her passion, Ms. Generic_Name has become one of the leading experts in her field. No one should be satisfied with knowing just what they currently understand; instead, people should actively pursue more knowledge related to their interests, just as she did.

Some may argue that a person can continue to grow by mastering just one skill, focusing only on their passion or chosen career. For example, Generic_Name dreamed of becoming a builder and completed his studies in construction. However, he did not become exactly what he hoped for; he could have become an architect but chose a simpler path. Despite this, people should aim to keep learning new things instead of limiting themselves to one mastery. It is possible to be an expert in one area, but it is important to stay open to continuous learning every day.

In conclusion, individuals will not truly grow if they do not venture beyond what they already know. A person's knowledge grows with time and curiosity. Since knowledge is closely linked to growth, it is better to achieve mastery in one field but remain open to gaining more knowledge continuously.

Some say that first impressions are nearly impossible to alter. I disagree with this idea. People’s impressions can shift not only because individuals grow and develop over time, but also due to the influence of others and the way life’s experiences affect them.

One reason first impressions can change is that people mature as they grow older. For instance, my mother often tells me that I am very different now compared to when I was a child. She points out how both my appearance and behavior have transformed because I have grown up. When I was seven or eight, I was shy and careful to avoid trouble by being polite. At that age, no one would dare to act out or behave badly if they cared about what others thought. This shows that as people mature, the way others see them can also change.

Another factor is the impact that the people around us have on our behavior and impressions. For example, my younger brother used to be very shy and quiet when speaking to others. However, after observing how I talked with confidence and calmness, he learned to do the same. Now, he is able to communicate easily and enjoy spending time with friends. This demonstrates that the people we interact with can influence how others perceive us, sometimes changing their initial impression completely.

Life experiences themselves also play a role in changing how people are perceived. For example, just before my 14th birthday, my father was arrested. I felt upset and did not want to celebrate because I believed life was unfair. At school, most people thought I was always happy and cheerful, but after they saw my reaction to my father’s arrest, their view of me changed. They noticed I was no longer joking or smiling, and instead, I seemed withdrawn and serious. As a result, rather than greeting me as usual, they gave me space, understanding that I was going through a difficult time. This shows how life’s challenges can alter people’s impressions of us.

In conclusion, the idea that first impressions cannot be changed is mistaken. People’s impressions can evolve over time due to personal growth, the influence of others, and life’s ups and downs. These factors reveal that no one’s initial impression is fixed, as life and relationships continually shape how we are seen by others.

There is no doubt that students put in a lot of effort in their studies. Between school assignments, homework, extracurricular activities, and sometimes part-time jobs, their lives can become quite overwhelming. Because of this, it is crucial for students to have a period of rest every now and then. I firmly believe that students should have an extended summer vacation rather than attending school throughout the entire year. This is because, first, there are many valuable activities during summer that help keep their minds engaged; second, their health is at risk without sufficient breaks; and finally, a long summer holiday also benefits school staff.

Everyone needs occasional breaks from their routine in order to relax, enjoy life, and perhaps discover new passions. While education is essential for future success, experiences outside the classroom also play a vital role in developing important life skills. During the summer holiday, students have the opportunity to participate in various activities such as sports, camps, or summer jobs, which keep both their minds and bodies active. Although these activities may not involve traditional studying, they encourage critical thinking, open-mindedness, and teamwork—skills necessary for real-world situations. For instance, imagine a student at a summer camp working with unfamiliar peers on a challenging problem that requires cooperation, analytical thinking, and empathy towards others’ viewpoints. This mirrors the collaborative environment found at school, showing that students can remain mentally stimulated even outside formal education.

While some students might not engage in structured activities during summer, the break still offers essential relief from daily pressures. Throughout the school year, students face numerous demands that can negatively affect their mental well-being. Recent years have seen a rise in depression among teenagers, and although not solely caused by school stress, it certainly contributes to it. Excessive workload and pressure negatively influence overall health, leading to issues like high blood pressure, weight changes, and more. Additionally, stress triggers the release of cortisol, a hormone that, when in excess, can hinder cognitive function and reaction time. Since students need clear thinking to perform well academically, a lack of rest may lead to poorer grades and worsening mental health.

Moreover, summer vacation is a necessary time for everyone involved in education, including teachers, administrators, and counselors. Schools exist to educate students, but this is only possible because of the efforts of school employees. They deserve time off as much as the students do because they face similar stressors during the academic year. A long break allows teachers to carefully plan lessons and also enjoy personal time with family and friends. After all, educators are human too and need the chance to recharge and forget about the heavy workload and comparatively low salaries.

In conclusion, I strongly support the idea of having an extended summer break rather than a year-round school schedule. Summer offers students opportunities to engage in activities that develop important cognitive and social skills. It also provides them with a chance to reduce stress and protect their mental and physical health. Lastly, a lengthy summer holiday is just as crucial for school staff to rest and rejuvenate, benefiting the whole education community.

There is a famous quote by the renowned artist Michelangelo: "The greater danger for most of us lies not in setting our aim too high and falling short, but in setting our aim too low and achieving our mark." Although some people might disagree, aiming higher is generally more beneficial. When people set ambitious goals, they are more likely to accomplish greater things. Additionally, aiming high encourages more original ideas compared to those who limit themselves by setting low targets. It also opens up various opportunities in different directions.

To begin with, setting ambitious goals can lead to many possibilities. People often decide their aims before they start working or thinking about their future. For instance, which choice would give you more career opportunities: applying only for dishwashing jobs because they are easy, or applying to many different fields for which you are qualified? The same principle applies to education. For example, a student who is unsure about their future might opt to join the military or attend college where many options are available. Going to college generally provides more job opportunities and the chance to find a better career compared to joining the military.

Moreover, aiming high helps individuals develop more unique and authentic ideas compared to those who have limited thinking and set low goals. People with low aims often hide or are unaware of their true potential. They tend to avoid challenges, which restricts their thinking and creativity. On the other hand, people who strive for difficult goals challenge themselves and think more deeply. This mental effort helps the brain develop in novel ways. Many famous artists who created remarkable works of art did so because they refused to set limits on their abilities. Their high ambitions allowed them to produce unique ideas and masterpieces.

In addition, aiming for higher goals often results in greater achievements than settling for easier targets. For instance, consider working on a school assignment: will doing just the minimum be as rewarding as putting in maximum effort? Most likely not. If you set your aim too low, you might give up before completing an important task. However, having high ambitions pushes you to persist and succeed. Therefore, aiming higher is better than choosing the easiest path.

Some might argue that having very high goals can cause unnecessary stress and suffering. While this can be true to some extent, it does not mean that aiming low is the right choice. The key is to maintain a balanced approach. Just like a balanced diet is essential for good health, setting realistic but challenging goals is crucial to personal growth. Some people say that aiming low helps them avoid stress and work less hard. Although this might reduce stress, not all stress is harmful. Sometimes stress can motivate people to improve. For example, when I was a student in Japan, I hated school and was too lazy to do my work. I felt stressed and ended up staying at home, which did not help me feel better at all. Eventually, I decided to return to school because I realized some stress can be beneficial.

In conclusion, avoiding challenges and taking the easy route is not always the best decision. Although aiming low may seem safe and simple, the real risk lies in forgetting to aim high and believing in your ability to achieve great things. The best approach is to make thoughtful decisions and set the best possible goals you can. Nobody has to be perfect or outstanding, but everyone should give their best effort in life so they have no regrets when it ends.

Being true to yourself brings out the best in a person. When you stay genuine, you don’t have to pretend to be someone else. Although some changes in life are necessary, you should never lose your true self by becoming a worse version of who you are. Your personality and attitude define you, and these qualities are what make you stand out. Many people change because they want to improve or because they are tired of being quiet and reserved. However, the way you act reflects the kind of person you are, and trying to revert back to someone you no longer feel like can be very challenging since it means altering your own nature.

First of all, being yourself means embracing your uniqueness. You don’t need to change just to prove something to others. Even if you have flaws like being rude or disrespectful, those are still part of who you are. Change often happens due to life’s difficult experiences, such as losing a loved one, facing abuse, or struggling with depression. These events can deeply affect your personality. Yet, by being yourself and willingly trying to improve, you can make significant progress, even if your family or friends are used to the “old you.” If you decide to change, let it be because you want to become better, not because you want to avoid being talked about negatively. Remember, it’s important to care less about what others think because no one can truly change who you are.

Secondly, changing too much can make you lose your inner self. You should only change for your own benefit, not to please others like friends, who may not always value who you really are. Your actions and personality reflect your true character. My grandmother used to tell me, “Sweetie, always be yourself because no one will love and respect you like your family.” No matter how annoying or difficult you can be, you are still an important part of your family. You shouldn’t feel pressured to change just because some people think negatively of you. Instead, reveal your true self, because inside you might have qualities that haven’t been seen yet. Many people may try to bring you down by gossiping or encouraging others to dislike you just because you are quiet or misunderstood. Be proud of your individuality and show everyone that you are confident with who you already are.

Thirdly, your personality represents your character. Nobody wants to be friends with someone who acts superior or arrogant. It’s important to stay true to your roots, even if you don’t have fancy things or a beautiful home. Showing that you don’t care about others’ judgments proves your confidence and authenticity. Don’t become someone you might regret being, because pretending to be different can harm your relationships. If a friend or family member stops talking to you, don’t respond by becoming mean or unkind, as this will only push them further away. Also, don’t be afraid to accept advice from others who want to help you become better. Aim to be the person known for being genuine, not someone who copies others or loses their true identity. I have never wanted to be just popular or well-known; I want to be respected for being myself.

Lastly, trying to go back to a previous version of yourself after you’ve changed can be very hard. Once you have moved on from who you used to be, it might be too late to return because those changes have created a new path in your life. People who once distanced themselves might never come back after you changed your personality. The things you did to change yourself could have lasting effects that can’t simply be reversed. So, instead of trying to become someone you were before, accept who you have become. You made changes for a reason, and it’s important to embrace them and love the person you are becoming. The choices you make about who you want to be now will shape your future as you grow older.

In conclusion, always be yourself and avoid changing into someone you’re not. Who you are today can influence the rest of your life. While it’s okay to adjust sometimes, never do it just for people who don’t deserve to see the real you. Strive to be unique and true to yourself, as many people will appreciate and enjoy your company for who you genuinely are. By being authentic, you pave the way for the person you want to become as you grow and eventually leave your family’s home.

When seeking advice, it is unlikely that you will rely on just one person. Ideally, you consult multiple people to weigh different perspectives and reduce the chance of missing better opportunities. Many individuals prefer to gather opinions from several sources instead of depending entirely on one person's viewpoint.

Choosing among several alternatives can be overwhelming, and there is always a risk that the choice you make could lead to either an excellent or disastrous outcome. Making such decisions is often difficult and can put a lot of pressure on you.

In conclusion, talking to multiple people when seeking advice offers a variety of benefits by exposing you to different options and experiences. I believe in the importance of individuality. I appreciate when people choose what they want for themselves because life becomes much more enjoyable that way. I have many friends, and they often follow what others do. However, I prefer to do what I am told and what I personally enjoy, rather than simply copying others.

My family can be quite negative at times, which I dislike because I want to express myself, but they do not want to listen. This is why I value individuality—I want others to hear me and allow me to pursue what I desire.

I have noticed that many people depend too much on others, and I think that is not a good habit.

In history class, we learned a lot about how people in the past lacked individuality.

I believe people seek attention, which is why they rely on others.

Life today is very different from the past because now people are influenced by what others say about how they look or what they think of them.

I like who I am because I am a kind person with positive qualities, so I do whatever I want since I appreciate myself and don’t worry about others’ opinions.

Now, since I am not sure what else to write, I will share a bit about my life. I arrived from Puerto Rico two years ago, and since then, my life has changed completely.

I started to appreciate everything I have because now I understand the value and sacrifice needed to achieve anything.

Despite everything, I still want to improve myself and grow in many ways.

It hasn’t been easy because the language and customs are very different.

But I am here and will continue to be because I believe in myself, and I know that whenever I set a goal, I accomplish it.

It’s not easy to arrive and meet people from different places—some are really good, and others not so much.

I really enjoy learning new things and visiting new places. However, one thing that upsets me is that even though I am not undocumented and Puerto Ricans are part of the United States, many people treat us as if we were undocumented just because Spanish is our first language.

In these two years, school has been one of my biggest challenges because it is hard to enter a classroom and feel completely alone.

Since I cannot ask questions or communicate well with others, I just stay quiet and watch others progress while I struggle.

A few months after arriving from Puerto Rico, I started skipping school and making bad choices because I had no support, neither at school nor at home.

Today, sometimes I feel like I don’t belong here. The only reason I stay is because of my mom—I want her to succeed and provide her with everything she deserves.

When we needed her, she was always there, and despite how difficult life was in Puerto Rico, she always tried to give us the best.

Thomas Jefferson said, "Do we accomplish more if we are always doing something, or does inactivity also serve a purpose?" Furthermore, not all people agree with this statement. Of course, those two persons have different ideas. Furthermore, many people like to be lazy, and they do not try to move on; since others want to move and work hard to make more opportunities. I agree with this statement, because this represents three nice ways to make others' opportunities: struggle, exploit, and relate.

However, not everyone agrees. To begin, some people think they can't make more options than they already have for some reasons. For instance, a lot of people have not an easy life; some of them are not rich and do not have money to make more options. But, we have to know something that's true about this life: that nothing is going to be easy to make or do. For instance, one day before my grandfather died, he told me a story about how things were before in his life. His life was really hard before; his family was not rich, and his five children only ate one time on some days. But he always said these words, "One day everything is going to change." He never stopped believing that. After this terrible day, he found other opportunities to make a different life for his family. That is why every day I think carefully, if you want something, "I need to struggle."

Moreover, we can accomplish wonderful dreams if we exploit the time. For instance, people can make many dreams come true fast, also things you never believed to get one day like a beautiful car, a big house, and other beautiful things. But you can get all of these if you work hard. In addition, other people can have a different life because you know how to help others. All the persons who never stop working always make so many things.

Finally, being related every day is something special. Because you are always looking for something more than one. That means you do not stop on one street; you always try to cross to the other way. For instance, one day I was thinking about how to make my dream fast and how to get it. And I said, "If we are people who like to find different options, we are going to get it." And that is all; this is a reflection to know how you can get everything in your life, but you have to know this: if you never go in, nothing is going to happen.

In short, the idea is to tell you how many opportunities or dreams you can make if you move from one side to the other side. For example, people who do not try to move farther away are never going to make something different, and that is so sad because you are never going to know how many special dreams you can have. But that is going to happen if you don't move to the other side. If you work hard and always look for more, you are always going to have everything in your life. For instance, you want a car, and the car costs one million; you will buy that car. Why? Because you worked hard and you have the money, so you will have the money to buy these types of cars. Struggle and you will have everything you want; exploit, go outside, and find other opportunities. Do not lose your time; time runs very fast every day. This example shows that such a change would negatively impact not only me but also many other students who have commitments outside of school.

Secondly, having longer school hours would be very exhausting for students. Classes would last much longer than usual, causing students to become tired and lose focus during lessons. Moreover, students would have less time and energy to do their homework in the evening since they would arrive home late and need to rest for the next day. As a result, their academic performance might suffer because they may not complete assignments on time.

Some people also argue that increasing the length of the school day could lead to lower attendance rates. Students might skip school more often due to tiredness from the extended hours, which would be harmful since regular attendance is crucial for passing the school year.

In conclusion, although there would be fewer school days each week, having school days that are two hours longer would be difficult for students to manage. As a student, I believe this change would disrupt my routine, cause stress, and negatively affect both attendance and grades. Therefore, I do not support the idea of extending the school day to fit a four-day week model.

I disagree with distance learning as a preferred method for education. First, students may not benefit from studying at home since they lack immediate support when they do not understand something. Without a teacher or classmates nearby, it can be difficult to clarify doubts or get help quickly.

Secondly, being physically present at school is important to fully grasp what you need to learn as a student. School provides an environment specifically designed for education, which helps students focus and absorb the material better than at home.

Finally, although it is possible to learn through distance education, attending classes in person at school remains the most effective way to gain knowledge. Direct interaction with teachers and peers fosters a better learning experience.

While some schools offer distance learning because it suits certain students, not all students find it beneficial. Many have responsibilities after school, such as work or taking care of family, which can make studying from home difficult. For example, immigrants who move to a new country often face the challenge of learning a new language while also supporting themselves financially. For them, balancing distance learning with other duties can be especially hard.

On the other hand, online classes can be a great opportunity for some students who have valid reasons to study from home. For instance, students with children might not be able to attend school in person, so they rely on distance learning as the only way to pursue their education. These students need motivation to keep working towards their goals, and with enough determination, they can succeed.

In my opinion, many students are not well-suited to learning from home because there are too many distractions, such as electronic devices or family members, which can prevent concentration.

Video conferencing can help some students study remotely, but it has its limitations. If a student has questions or is confused, it is harder to get immediate answers compared to being in a classroom. For this reason, attending school in person remains the best approach. Putting in consistent effort every day at school prepares students for their future. We are responsible for our actions, and the outcomes we face depend on the choices we make.

When you share your story and the efforts you made, they will respect you because only you have the power to develop your own character traits.

You can build yourself up and honor their memory by showing how much you have learned from your experience. Every day, you try to make the most of your time, proving that you are strong even when occasional sadness occurs. These struggles make your character stronger, even if you don’t always notice it yourself. Everyone faces moments of self-doubt and feels like giving up, thinking they are not capable of succeeding. But once you recognize what you have already achieved, the world seems less frightening. Your mind might try to convince you that something is impossible through negative thoughts, but focusing on these only holds you back. Your character exists to help you overcome difficulties and break through the obstacles life places in your path. You have the power to push past these barriers. So don’t hesitate to follow what you believe is right. Trust your instincts and let your heart guide you. Don’t let anyone or anything stop you from transforming what seems impossible into something real. Stand out by making your character unique because you are different, no matter what anyone thinks.

People have the freedom to make their own choices because they can pursue whatever they have been aiming for over time. No one enjoys doing something against their will, and everyone has the right to decide what they want to become or what path to take in life.

However, some decisions involve choosing between a difficult path or an easier one. The hard path requires working diligently, such as studying hard to achieve good grades or putting in effort at work. The easier path might involve investing money or resources at the beginning to fast-forward future opportunities. This shortcut is often challenging and not everyone can or wants to take it, depending on their circumstances. Where a person stands in life also plays a role. For instance, people who have a lot of money can make quicker decisions about their future since they do not worry much about financial obligations like taxes or bills. On the other hand, those with limited funds face a longer journey because they must handle many financial responsibilities, such as taxes and car payments, while working harder to achieve their goals. 

I once had a friend who was attending school while working at the same time. As he was about to graduate high school and move on to college, he made a poor choice. He decided to quit school because he believed that working was more profitable than continuing his studies. Now, he works in the nail industry, where his income is unstable. He is unwilling to try harder or return to college, even though pursuing higher education might have led to a better-paying job. This decision has affected his life significantly, and he cannot change it. Similarly, my brother attended college for two years before deciding to leave and start working. It is possible that if he had continued, he might have secured a better job. Sometimes, people need to carefully consider their future and plan based on what they currently have and what they expect to have. While individuals can make their own choices, they often need support from others when making important life decisions. Many people struggle because they are unsure about their interests or what career path to follow, making them feel stuck and in need of guidance.

The options people have and the experiences around them influence how they decide their future. Support from family and friends can help them make better choices. It is important to plan one's life, work hard, and strive for a comfortable future where they are free to do what they want. If people put in enough effort now, it will be easier for their children to make their own decisions later on.

Students should be permitted to bring their cell phones to school because there are situations where they might need to contact their parents urgently. For example, if a student faces an emergency or if their parents have an urgent situation, such as a car accident, they might want to inform their child about changes in pickup plans after school. For these reasons, school principals should allow students to bring cell phones but require them to be turned off during class.

In the hallways, phones should be used only in emergencies—for instance, if a student suddenly feels unwell or faints, another student could quickly call the nurse for assistance. Allowing controlled use of phones in these ways helps balance safety with minimizing distractions during school hours.

A current topic often discussed is whether energy and resources can be saved by changing work or school schedules. Some companies have moved to a four-day work week, with ten hours each day. This raises the question: should schools also extend their days by two hours following this model? While some people argue that lengthening the school day will actually waste more energy and resources—such as electricity, lighting, and water due to longer use— I believe schools should adopt this approach. By doing so, we can better protect our resources and gain more time to raise awareness about improving the world.

One reason I support extending the school day is that it can help us save energy in the long run. Schools can also use this opportunity to teach students how to use energy more responsibly, for example by educating them on how to reduce electricity consumption at home. These lessons can help students develop habits that lower their utility bills and minimize waste.

Another important resource that schools can help conserve is water. Since students often use the restroom multiple times a day and sometimes leave taps running, creating awareness is crucial. The school could put up posters to explain why saving water is important and encourage students to be more mindful. Additionally, schools can focus on reducing plastic and paper use, which are often purchased in large quantities. Saving money on these resources could help the school improve in other areas, and students would learn to take responsibility for the environment.

Finally, by adding two extra hours to the school day, teachers and students would have more time to participate in activities that promote sustainability. For example, they could organize campaigns to educate the community about climate change and ways to protect the environment. Students might also create an online platform to share tips on conserving resources, reaching people both inside and outside of school.

In conclusion, I believe schools should lengthen the school day by two hours because this change would increase awareness and encourage everyone to conserve energy and other resources. Most importantly, developing a stronger sense of responsibility can lead to a better world. Only when we become aware and decide to make changes will we see real improvements for the future.

In conclusion, I’d like to think that we create and build our own character and that we are not given a label by any higher power of what our character is going to be in life.

So honestly, I don't think that we’re born with labels. I feel like we all can make our own decisions about what we’re going to make of life. If you have a broken down, weak mindset, you’re going to have negative vibes and a weak, deadbeat character. But if you have a strong mindset and the will to get stuff done, then you’ll have a broad and respected character.

In conclusion, I’d like to think that we create and build our own character and that we are not given a label by any higher power about what our character is going to be in life.

At birth, the first thing we instinctively do is cry. If a newborn doesn’t cry, doctors often stimulate them to do so by gently tapping their backs. From that initial cry, each person develops their own unique sound and pitch. We also have unique fingerprints, which are never duplicated—even identical twins have different prints. As we grow, we begin to shape our own identities. Right after birth, our brains start to work, even in small ways. Babies soon learn to cry to signal hunger, discomfort, pain, or simply to seek attention.

As children move into toddlerhood, they gain new skills by observing those around them. They learn to walk by watching others, pick up language through listening, and figure out how to hold a bottle or use utensils by watching daily routines. All of these abilities come from imitation and observation. Between the ages of six and twelve, kids start to develop a desire to belong to groups and fit in with their peers. At this stage, they watch television and learn about different roles in society—like musicians, actors, firefighters, doctors, athletes, and many more. These images influence their understanding of what is possible.

During the teenage years, from 13 to 19, individuals begin to develop their own unique voices and identities, making choices independently. Parents are no longer constantly guiding every decision, although they often offer advice based on their own experiences. Sometimes, making mistakes is necessary for growth, as failure teaches valuable lessons about what works and what doesn’t.

Once adulthood arrives, the safety net of living under one’s parents disappears. Adults must take full responsibility for their choices and actions. Holding a job introduces new responsibilities, through which people learn whether they are disciplined, social, patient, forgiving, or otherwise. I believe that everyone is born with the potential to grow and adapt to society. How we behave depends largely on our experiences and mindset. For example, a person living in tough conditions might still maintain a positive outlook, while someone from a more comfortable background might focus on trivial complaints.

In my view, we are not born with fixed labels or predetermined characters. Instead, we have the freedom to decide what kind of life we want to lead. Attitude plays a huge role in shaping who we become. If a person adopts a negative, defeatist mindset, their character will likely reflect that. Conversely, a strong will and positive outlook can build a well-rounded and respected personality. To sum up, I believe that our character is something we create and develop ourselves, not a label assigned by any higher power.

On the positive side, technology can be a great help for people who feel lonely, allowing them to entertain themselves without needing someone else around. Loneliness can be very harmful to a person’s mental health, and while there are worse situations like imprisonment, unemployment, or death, many people would rather face those than be completely alone. Activities like reading books, shopping online, playing games, listening to music on apps like Pandora, or watching favorite shows on YouTube or Netflix are all examples of how technology can be used in a positive way to combat loneliness.

One negative effect of technology is that it can reduce people's interest in real-life social activities, such as family gatherings. Technology is undoubtedly one of the greatest inventions ever. It has made communication easier, provides endless entertainment, keeps us informed about global events—even space news—and saves us from reading long books just to find answers. It has simplified many tasks; for example, you can shop or order food without leaving your home.

Yet, this convenience has also made people more lazy. They might ask themselves, “Why should I do this when my phone or computer can do it for me?” or “Why should I meet someone in person to talk when I can just chat on my phone?” If this mindset continues, it might lead to having no one around in the future.

In conclusion, technology is a wonderful tool if used in moderation and only when necessary. It is important not to let it take over your mind or life completely.

Technology has both advantages and drawbacks when it comes to human interaction, but overall, it has had a mostly positive impact on people’s lives. In today’s world, technology is present almost everywhere and is used for various purposes. Without technology, we would have fewer opportunities to learn and grow. Additionally, it eliminates the need for face-to-face conversations, as advanced devices like phones allow us to communicate easily with people from different countries through texts or calls. Technology undoubtedly simplifies many aspects of life, and I believe its effects are generally beneficial. Here are some examples to support this view.

Technology plays a significant role in many areas of our lives, which leads to positive outcomes. For instance, many individuals rely on technology for their jobs. They can find answers to their questions independently without needing to consult others. Without these technological tools, some people might struggle to work or earn a living. In education, both teachers and students frequently use technology. Students often complete assignments on computers and submit them online, and they can quickly search for information on the internet. In U.S. schools, about half of the learning process involves technology, which has reduced dependence on traditional books. Similarly, doctors use various technological devices to assist in diagnosing and treating patients. Modern tools enable safer and more successful operations, saving more lives than in the past when doctors relied only on textbooks. On the other hand, technology also helps industries like manufacturing, reducing the need for hard physical labor by automating tasks that were once done manually.

People can use technology in positive or negative ways. Over time, many have learned how to use it responsibly and effectively. Most users apply technology to support their work, such as secretaries, teachers, and medical professionals, who use it for communication and data storage. In some Latin American countries, technology is sometimes seen as a “new babysitter” because parents use devices like phones or tablets to entertain their children while they attend to other tasks. However, not all uses are good. Some individuals misuse technology to commit fraud, stalk others on social media, or engage in online scams. There have been cases where children and elderly people fall victim to these crimes, which can be very serious, even fatal. Additionally, some people become hackers, stealing sensitive data like bank information without caring who is harmed. These examples show that although there are many good uses of technology, not everyone chooses to use it in positive ways.

Technology also influences how people live and think. For example, it increases personal safety by providing advanced home security systems. Moreover, it offers new opportunities for self-expression, such as through social media platforms, where people like YouTubers can share their interests with a wide audience—even though they may not know their viewers personally. Older generations have also changed how they communicate; instead of writing letters, they can easily send texts or make video calls. Although there are limits to communication without physical presence, these technologies still allow people to stay connected. Online gaming, for instance, enables players from different countries to interact and speak face-to-face through their devices, which enhances social interaction despite physical distance. Hence, technology positively addresses some limitations in human contact.

In conclusion, while technology can limit direct human interaction, it also brings many benefits. In the workplace, personal communication with colleagues is important to maintain good relationships. Similarly, in romantic relationships, verbal conversations are necessary for a strong connection, not just texting. However, technology also enables collaborative learning and communication among classmates and friends, making it easier to find answers and share knowledge. Overall, both human contact and technology have their positive and negative sides. Sometimes, people rely on technology instead of books due to convenience, but technology does not always provide accurate information. Despite its usefulness, I believe maintaining face-to-face communication is essential and should not be replaced entirely by technology-based interaction.

There is an ongoing debate about whether students should have to choose a career path when they start high school. Many schools encourage students to pick courses that lead toward a particular profession. However, I believe it is not a good idea for young students to decide on a career so early because they often lack the maturity and experience to make the right choice.

One important reason against this is that many students are simply too young to fully understand what a specific career involves. High school students usually have little to no real-world experience to help them make informed decisions about their future jobs.

In my opinion, it is better to wait until later in high school, such as junior or senior year, before deciding on a career. This allows students time to explore different options and select the courses that best prepare them for their chosen field.

Another reason this early commitment is problematic is that teenagers can be careless or change their minds as they grow older. For example, the classes a student picks in their freshman year might no longer suit them by the time they reach senior year. I know a friend who started with a technology class but later discovered that the salary in that field was not what he expected. He switched his focus to materials and processes, learning skills related to building houses instead.

Also, making a career decision at a young age can sometimes lead to mistakes. I believe the smartest approach is to wait, study a broad range of useful classes, and carefully consider the best options for a future career. To do this successfully, students need to be responsible and take their education seriously.

In conclusion, it is clear that the best plan for students is to concentrate on doing well in high school and not rush into choosing a career too soon. By the time they reach senior year or start college, they will have a better understanding of life and work. That is the ideal moment to select courses that will help guide them toward a specific profession.

A lot of people suggest leaving the found object where it is because the owner will come back looking for it; no one leaves their belongings behind on purpose without caring. Many kids followed these rules, but some didn’t care, and that’s not acceptable. Some people don’t need the items they take—they just want them. Needing something means it’s really important to you, and without it, you would struggle. If you truly need something, you can usually buy it from a nearby shop. Wanting something, on the other hand, means you don’t have to have it, but you desire it for fun, to show off, or just because you feel like taking it, even though you don’t need it or face any hardship.

If you find something, don’t take it. If you see someone drop an item, return it to them. Always think about your actions. Don’t give in to peer pressure. Be helpful and kind.

The idea of having a four-day school week has sparked much discussion, weighing its advantages and disadvantages. Instead of attending school for five regular days, some suggest replacing that with just four extended days of classes.

Adopting a four-day week is an option that should be considered not only by employees in various businesses but also by high schools and colleges after reviewing the following reasons.

While a four-day schedule means losing ten hours of class time each week, those hours can be recovered by lengthening the school day by two hours and increasing the duration of each lesson. This approach can improve focus during classes and allow students more time to complete projects or assignments. With those extra two hours, students would also have additional opportunities to spend time with classmates and teachers for support, especially for those struggling in certain subjects.

Another possibility is dedicating the extra time on the fourth day to activities like library work, which would appeal to students who enjoy reading or those wanting to spend more time on sports or other extracurricular activities.

The fifth day of the week could then serve for doctor appointments or other health-related matters, reducing the need for students to miss regular classes. Currently, parents sometimes write notes explaining absences, but having this day free would minimize interruptions to learning.

It is important to remember teachers who are also parents and could benefit from an extra day to spend with their families or attend to personal responsibilities.

Seniors, who face important decisions about their future, including choosing universities or jobs, would gain valuable time to explore these options. Freshmen, who transition from middle to high school, also need support adjusting to new routines and activities.

The free day—whether Friday or Monday—could be used for community service, with parental permission and adult supervision. Students interested could volunteer to clean streets, rivers, or take part in other community projects. Schools might even partner with large companies to offer students part-time job opportunities during this free day and on weekends.

This model would mean attending school only four full days each week, giving students three days off to spend with family or friends or to rest and handle other commitments. Depending on the school’s decision, the free day could be on Friday or Monday, allowing for a longer weekend or a more relaxed start to the week.

Although this schedule might not suit students with part-time jobs, extending the school day by two hours could reduce their available work hours during weekdays. However, the extra free day offers the chance to work full-time or part-time on that day and weekends.

Balancing school and work every day can be tiring and leave little time for rest. With only four school days, even if those days are longer, students would have time after classes to relax and complete homework, plus three days to work or manage other activities.

Despite some challenges, most concerns can be addressed, and for over 90% of students, the benefits outweigh the disadvantages.

After considering all points, I conclude that everyone deserves three days off from school and only four days of classes. Whether students use their free day to stay home, spend time with family, help at home, work, or study, if we all agree on this change, together we have the power to advocate for this new right for high school and college students. United, we can make it happen.

Some schools organize programs that involve both younger and older students. These initiatives aim to help both groups understand their responsibilities and support each other. Older students learn how to guide and assist the younger ones, while younger students get a clearer idea of what to expect as they grow older. In this way, both benefit from the exchange.

Older students can share their experiences and explain the mistakes they have made. Since everyone makes different errors, they can help younger students avoid similar problems and encourage them to make better choices. This mutual learning enables them to support one another effectively.

Younger students can also recognize their own mistakes through these programs. Older students often visit younger ones to offer advice and share life lessons, guiding them to make the right decisions. This interaction helps the younger students develop and learn from both their own and others’ experiences.

Younger students rely on older students much like older students depend on adults. Older students can warn younger ones about what actions to avoid and help solve their problems. For example, some younger students may struggle with English, and older students can assist them. Meanwhile, older students might ask younger students for help in certain situations. Together, they can cooperate and accomplish many things. Sometimes, if conflicts arise among younger students, older ones can step in to calm the situation and encourage positive behavior. Everyone makes mistakes, but by helping each other, the students learn and grow. The main difference between them is that older students usually have more responsibilities, while younger ones have fewer demands placed on them.

My father once told me that when he was young, he needed help but was hesitant to ask an older person. He advised me to seek assistance from older students whenever I face difficulties, so I can avoid mistakes and learn from them. Older students play an important role by guiding younger students to understand life better. Because older students have more experience, they can teach younger ones what is right or wrong, encouraging harmony between the two groups. However, a big problem can occur if older students refuse to help younger ones.

There can also be challenges between these two groups. Sometimes, older students do not want to support younger students, and younger students may refuse to listen. This creates difficulties because, while older students try to share important lessons, the younger ones might ignore them. Similarly, older students may resist listening to adults or teachers, which causes further problems. When someone tells us not to do something, sometimes we do it even more, and when consequences come, we regret it. That’s why it is necessary for older students to guide younger ones and help them understand what is good or bad. Just as older students need adults for advice, younger students need older students’ support. They can protect each other and grow together in a positive way.

One activity I consider really enjoyable is science experiments. One of the reasons I consider these activities fun is because they are different from other types of projects. And what I mean by this is that, for example, when one does a math project or a language arts project, it is nothing more than doing many math exercises or writing an essay. Unlike the science projects, for example, one time I got to see a frog's interior. And it might sound disgusting to many of the people reading this, and to be honest, it didn't smell good either. But one of the things that fascinated me about the project was that frogs don't have as many organs as we humans do. Or maybe they removed some of them, but there weren't a lot of organs in there.

And another thing I was curious about was that they were different colors. I remember seeing blue and pink; unlike us humans, almost all of our insides are red. Frogs actually have different colors in their interior, but they looked a little dry because my teacher told me that they had been frozen for some time. But it definitely made it easier to cut parts in the interior of the frog. And also, since my teacher told me that we were able to cut whatever we wanted, my group and I tried to explore as much as possible. But there was a part that was really disgusting, which was that there were some flies in the frog's stomach. And that part definitely disgusted me, but it didn't make me want to stop either.

After we finished trying to see everything inside the frog, the teacher told us the name and function of each of the parts of the frog. But one of my friends decided it was silly to poke the frog's eye. And until this point, I still don't know what went through his mind at that exact moment. But when he poked it, it turned out that the frog's eye wasn't completely frozen, so liquid from the eye just came rushing out and he got wet because he decided to do that. Fortunately, it didn't reach me, but it definitely reached my mate. After that, the teacher sent him to the bathroom to wash himself.

After that happened, my teacher decided that it was best to just stop the project. But it was definitely a lot of fun.

Another example of a project was recently when my teacher decided to have us do a project in the dark because it is themed to what we are learning about right now, which is the unit of light. The project was really simple and, to be honest, it wasn't as amazing and funny as the other project. But it was to spray a liquid in front of a flashlight. And what was supposed to happen was that I would be able to see the waves on which light travels. And after the teacher explained the process of how this happens, she told us to spray the liquid in front of the flashlight and, being honest, I didn't see anything. I was kind of disappointed. But after four seconds, I could see them, and they were kind of hard to see, and it was for just a few seconds, but I actually enjoyed the project. But it had some downsides like it was really short and the teacher took forever to explain the process. But I still think it was a really interesting project.

And what I tried to show by giving you these examples from my own personal experiences is that science experiments are not always boring and you may not like them, but you should give them a chance. And I promise you that you are going to like them or at least one of the many projects there are. Because they make class a little more interesting. And in my opinion, projects or experiments are the best activities there are in school. Because they teach you in a more direct type of learning. And that's why I think they are the best.
