One activity I find truly enjoyable is conducting science experiments. One reason I think these activities are fun is that they differ from other types of school projects. For example, when working on a math project or a language arts assignment, you mostly just do a lot of exercises or write essays. Science projects, however, are usually more hands-on and exciting. One time, I had the chance to examine the inside of a frog. This might sound gross to many people, and honestly, it didn’t smell very pleasant either. But what fascinated me about this project was discovering that frogs don’t have as many organs as humans do. Maybe some organs were missing because of the way the frog was prepared, but there definitely weren’t many organs inside.

Another thing I found interesting was the different colors inside the frog. I remember seeing blue and pink parts, which is very different from humans since most of our internal organs are red. The frog’s organs looked a bit dry because, as my teacher explained, the frog had been frozen for a while. Still, this made it easier to cut into different parts. Since my teacher gave us permission to dissect wherever we wanted, my group and I tried to explore as much as possible. There was one part that I found really disgusting, though — the frog’s stomach contained some flies. That definitely grossed me out, but it didn’t make me want to stop.

After we finished exploring the frog, the teacher told us the names and functions of each organ we had seen. However, one of my friends thought it would be funny to poke the frog’s eye. I still don’t know what he was thinking in that moment. When he poked the eye, it wasn’t completely frozen, so liquid suddenly squirted out and got him wet. Luckily, it didn’t reach me, but it definitely splashed on my friend. The teacher then sent him to the bathroom to wash up.

Because of that incident, the teacher decided it was best to end the project early. Even so, it was definitely a lot of fun.

Another project we did recently was related to the unit on light. Our teacher had us work in the dark, which was different and related to what we were studying. This project was quite simple, and to be honest, it wasn’t as exciting as the frog dissection. The task was to spray a liquid in front of a flashlight. The idea was that we would be able to see the light waves traveling through the liquid. After the teacher explained how this happens, we tried it. At first, I couldn’t see anything, which was a bit disappointing. But then, after about four seconds, faint waves appeared for a short time. I actually enjoyed the project, although it was quite brief, and the teacher took a long time explaining the theory. Still, I found it interesting.

Through these examples from my own experiences, I want to show that science experiments are not always boring. Even if you think you won’t like them, you should give them a try. I promise you’ll enjoy at least one of the many projects available because they make classes more engaging. In my opinion, experiments and projects are the best school activities because they offer a more direct way of learning. That’s why I believe science experiments are the most rewarding.

The prompt says, "Unless you try something beyond what you have mastered, you will never grow." One would say that is something very wise to say. If I wish to try something new and be a better person in society, I will, but if I wish to not try anything at all and just do the same boring routine day after day, sooner or later I will get bored of everything. Even though some may argue by saying, "That's how I got successful in the first place, by doing the same routine over and over." In some cases, that may work. Author Ralph Waldo Emerson was a wise man to say, "Unless you try something beyond what you already have mastered, you will never grow."

However, many people overlook such wisdom, making it less impactful in everyday life. Personally, I agree with this idea. To illustrate this, in my ceramics class, the teacher mostly gives us examples of how to make clay items. However, she almost never helps me directly, and this makes it difficult for me and others to create things because she only explains the process once, and some students forget the instructions. When she helps someone, their project usually becomes the best in the class due to her assistance.

Some people say that receiving examples sometimes confuses them. This happens when the examples change their perspective on what they are doing. For example, when drawing, the teacher might say, "Make a drawing from your imagination," meaning from your own thoughts and whatever is in your mind. But if the teacher then gives examples of what to draw after saying the drawing should be from your imagination, this can make you think she wants you to draw something other than what you were imagining. This shows that sometimes examples do not work for certain subjects because they cause confusion.

Others say that using examples helps them influence others more effectively because examples show experience and teach how to do something. Many people learn better and are more influenced when examples are used. I think, however, that there are a few stronger ways to influence others that make examples less useful or even powerless. For these reasons, I believe there are better ways to influence people without using examples.

Have you ever wondered whether learning through examples is the best method, or if different approaches might be more effective? Albert Schweitzer once said, "Example is not the main thing to influence others," suggesting that there are alternative ways to impact people beyond simply providing examples.

One method of influence is offering direct assistance rather than just showing examples. This can sometimes be more effective. For instance, in my ceramics class, the teacher often demonstrates how to create clay objects, but usually does not offer much personal help. This approach makes it hard for me and some classmates to succeed because the instructions are given only once, and many students forget the steps. However, when the teacher does give individual support, those students tend to produce the best projects. This shows that personalized help can be more valuable than just demonstrating examples.

Some people also feel confused when given examples, especially if these examples make them question what they are doing. For example, when asked to draw something from their imagination, students might get mixed signals if the teacher then provides specific drawing examples. This can lead them to think the teacher expects something different from their own ideas. In such cases, examples don’t always help and may actually cause confusion, proving that examples might not work well in every situation.

On the other hand, some argue that examples allow people to share their experience and teach others how to do something, making them an effective way to influence learners. It is true that many individuals do respond well to example-based learning. However, I believe there are stronger techniques that limit the effectiveness of examples or even make them unnecessary. For these reasons, I think there are better ways to influence others without relying mainly on examples.

It doesn’t have to be taken too seriously, but having a hobby or sport you care about is valuable. Secondly, sports can be challenging since they require skill and dedication, which helps build strength and character. Finally, spending all day on electronics isn’t beneficial, so participating in an activity is a much better way to spend time. Life is short, so taking part in something you enjoy is essential. My second reason is that everyone should be involved in some activity because being lazy won’t bring success. When you spend your time doing nothing or avoiding effort, you don’t grow. Playing sports or joining activities keeps your body healthy, and it might even lead you to play professionally, which is very exciting. Staying active all the time helps your body develop and keeps you strong, which is why I strongly recommend doing some kind of sports or physical activity.

The third reason is that spending too much time on electronic devices is distracting and unhealthy. If you want to improve in an activity, you need to practice rather than being glued to your phone. A first impression is something that stays with people and is hard to forget. It can involve attitudes, feelings, or emotions, but once formed, it rarely changes. Whether it’s the way we behave, talk, walk, or even eat, these aspects tend to remain consistent. For instance, if someone has been in love with a girl since childhood, no matter how many new people come into the picture, that initial impression of love will not easily be replaced or erased.

When we make a first impression on others, even if they try to imitate or alter it later, it is nearly impossible to completely change it. Everyone understands that first impressions are not easily modified. For example, imagine a person tries to impress a friend with a special dish. The friend loves the taste and attempts to recreate it. Although the dish might look similar, it will never taste exactly the same because the friend does not know all the ingredients or the subtle details used. This shows how first impressions, like that dish, cannot be fully changed or copied in the same way.

We understand that first impressions are almost impossible to alter because they are like feelings that deeply affect us. Sometimes impressions are used to impress others and may not even be genuine—they can be false or exaggerated, but we might still believe them. For example, if a student lies about their personality or family to gain acceptance from friends, those impressions might be believed, but over time, it becomes clear they are not real. This further proves how first impressions, even if based on falsehoods, are difficult to change.

It is important to accept that first impressions are hard to change. We should trust ourselves and avoid trying to change other people's initial judgments or copying them. Attempting to redo or alter a first impression can be frustrating and painful, and even if we try our best, it will never be exactly the same as before.

Although our natural traits may have a strong influence, I believe they don’t fully determine who we become. Instead, people can take control over how they develop, even if it might seem beyond their reach at times.

It is not always true that the way others perceive us causes us to feel insecure or forces us to change. Often, the changes we make come from trying to improve ourselves, not just from our parents or family but also from society around us. Nowadays, there are many influences from the internet and other places that can shape us in ways we might not expect. These influences are not always controlled by anyone, so they can often affect us without us realizing it. Still, there is a lot of information to choose from in the world, and it is important to find what suits us best and stick to it. Society constantly changes, offering new perspectives that affect us all.

For example, many rappers often talk about topics like girls and life that influence youth in different ways. This is concerning because for someone new to a place, there are many changes and strong influences coming from people in places like California, where I used to live. Artists and musicians often aim to reach as many people as possible to gain attention and success, which increases their influence worldwide.

Both children and adults are influenced by others, but we also have the power to choose which ideas affect us. We decide the path we want to take and the influences we follow. For this reason, I feel proud of the world we live in, as it offers us choices even amid many external pressures.

These threats often make us more aware and cautious due to the many influences encouraging fear for our safety. Behind every strong influence, there is a lot of thought and intention.

In the workplace, technology can be useful, but it often causes distractions. People are easily drawn away from their tasks when their favorite sports team is playing. They take out their phones to watch the game and end up neglecting their work. This leads to poor performance, which sometimes results in losing their jobs, leaving them to struggle with finding new employment and supporting themselves. If technology did not exist, these problems might not be so common. Sometimes, technology causes more harm than good.

Additionally, technology has led to more accidents than in the past. For example, drivers who text while behind the wheel often miss turns or hit other cars, causing serious accidents. These mistakes can lead to people losing their loved ones and being held responsible for the tragedy. Because of carelessness linked to technology, families suffer great losses.

In summary, technology has a negative influence on human life. It makes people less human, lazier, and weaker. Technology has reduced genuine human connections, and our excessive dependence on it has made us vulnerable. Without technology, we might be like cavemen, but relying on it too much is damaging our humanity.

Most students look forward to summer vacation because it is one of the most wonderful times of the year. During these months, students have the chance to spend quality time with their families and friends. Although some teachers argue that the summer break is too long and that students tend to forget what they learned when they return to school in the fall, I believe summer is a very special period.

Summer allows students to connect more deeply with their loved ones. Many parents work long hours from Monday to Saturday, and sometimes even on Sundays, leaving little time to be with their families. Therefore, summer break offers a unique opportunity for students to enjoy moments with the most important people in their lives.

Personally, I cherish summer vacation because it gives me a chance to create meaningful memories with my family and my faith. When school is out, I spend more time with my mother, who is a very important person to me. She supports me through good and bad times and offers valuable advice to help me avoid mistakes she experienced in the past. These summer moments help me grow not only in school but also in my work, church activities, and everyday life.

My mother plays a fundamental role in my life by encouraging me to be a good person and to do well in school. I also devote time to my spiritual growth during this period, learning about what truly matters and gaining guidance that helps me live better. I believe that the two months we have for summer vacation is a reasonable amount of time, especially since we spend about nine months in school.

When some educators say summer vacation is too long because students lose the information they learned, I disagree. Students retain knowledge from their schoolwork, projects, and homework—it stays in our minds and is important. It is not true that a shorter summer break would be better.

Some suggest having a year-round school schedule with only a few weeks off in summer, but I do not agree with this idea. A shorter summer means less time for enjoyment and for building relationships with family, especially since many parents also take their vacations at this time. Summer is meant to be a fun and relaxing period spent with parents, siblings, and other family members.

For me, having about two months of vacation plus a couple of weeks off is beneficial because it allows me to clear my mind and take a break from school responsibilities. I once experienced a time when I had so much schoolwork that I couldn’t enjoy family activities. My uncle reminded me that sometimes it’s important to step away from school to spend time with family and recharge. I learned that missing out on family moments to focus solely on schoolwork can lead to regret, as family is always there for you.

It’s crucial to make time for family, friends, and schoolwork, understanding that life is unpredictable and we never know when we might lose a loved one. When school is in session, focus on your studies, and when it’s time to be with family, give them your full attention. Organizing your time well allows you to balance these important parts of life.

I have changed how I manage my schedule. From Monday to Friday, I focus on education, and on weekends, I dedicate myself to my faith and family. This balance helps me share more quality time with those I care about.

Summer vacation is especially important because many students have parents who work long hours and only get to see them during these breaks. Having order in life and making time for everything is essential. While education teaches us valuable knowledge about nature, science, and the world, family remains the most precious treasure because they might not always be here.

I also believe teachers enjoy their summer holidays, using this time to relax and be with their families. When school resumes, reviewing previous lessons helps refresh what students learned, as most knowledge remains stored in the brain.

To sum up, a summer vacation of two months with a few extra weeks is perfect for enjoying life with the people who matter most. It’s a time to have fun, rest, and strengthen relationships. Therefore, teachers should not worry about summer being too long—it is a necessary and welcome break for students and educators alike. Enjoy your summer vacation!

The text discusses how first impressions can change over time. Its purpose is to inform readers about various factors that cause these initial opinions to shift and the effects this shift can have. The author uses examples and supportive ideas to help readers better understand the topic, ultimately emphasizing that impressions are not fixed and can evolve at any moment.

A first impression is the initial opinion we form when we meet someone or encounter something for the first time. This initial judgment may be true or false, but it is something only time can reveal as we get to know the person or situation more deeply.

Changes in first impressions can have either positive or negative consequences. Sometimes, what we initially see as good turns out to be bad, and vice versa. For example, when buying a car, it might look attractive from the outside, but a thorough mechanical inspection might reveal serious problems. On the other hand, you might hear negative things about a person from someone else but discover the opposite after having a conversation with them yourself.

Several factors influence why first impressions change, including mistaken opinions, disappointment, anger, or self-reflection. These emotions and thoughts can shape how we adjust our initial views. For instance, when we are angry, everything might seem unpleasant or irritating. Alternatively, we might reconsider and correct a false belief we once held.

In conclusion, first impressions are important but not always accurate. Opinions can shift over time, becoming better or worse. I believe it is wiser to wait before forming a strong judgment about someone or something, as first impressions can definitely change as time goes on.

I have experienced this myself, and staying after school means getting home very late, sometimes around 7 or 8 p.m., which is exhausting. Because of longer school hours, we might miss out on activities like soccer or other hobbies, which would be disappointing and tiring, especially if classes last 80 minutes or more.

Participants would have to spend more time doing assignments despite only gaining a little extra time in class. For teachers living far from school, longer workdays would also be very challenging. They would face heavy traffic during the evening rush hour and get home late, only to start grading and preparing for the next day. Then, early mornings would come again with very little rest, making the routine exhausting. I haven’t even started working yet, and just imagining that schedule feels overwhelming.

If adding half an hour to the school day is necessary, then the school schedule should shift to start later, maybe around 8 a.m., so that students don’t have to wake up so early. It would be much better to begin later and finish earlier, creating a more relaxed and happier environment for everyone. Waking up early and staying late is difficult, so adjusting the timing in this way would help improve moods and reduce stress.

Another point is that as 8th graders, our lunch break is already late, around 1:40 p.m. If the day is extended, lunch might be pushed to around 2:10 p.m. I really don’t want to be that hungry during class because it makes it hard to focus and can cause irritability. Having to pick up students late would be tiring for them as well.

Overall, increasing school hours would create more problems than benefits for students, teachers, parents, and bus drivers. It is better to keep the current schedule or make adjustments that do not add extra stress to everyone involved.

These first impressions create ideas, feelings, or opinions about others. Sometimes, people unintentionally hurt others’ feelings because they do not carefully consider the words they use. By the time they realize this and want to make amends, it might already be too late. Changing first impressions is very difficult because hurt feelings can lead to changes in relationships or people’s behavior.

First impressions can indeed wound someone emotionally. For example, just yesterday, I unintentionally hurt my sister’s feelings. We were discussing her upcoming wedding next April, planning for her big day and searching for a wedding dress online. I care about her deeply, like a second mother to me, and I wanted her to look stunning. However, when she showed me one dress, my immediate thought was that it was unattractive. I told her she would look like a skeleton in it because she is thin. I didn’t expect to hurt her with my first impression. Even though she liked the dress, I only wanted her to wear the most beautiful one. After realizing my mistake, I apologized, but she was still upset. For a short time, she even stopped talking to me. I felt sad and reached out to apologize again, and eventually, she forgave me. This incident showed me that people often receive what we say at face value. Similarly, at a friend’s birthday party, one of her friends insulted me by calling me ugly and slow in front of others. Those harsh first impressions were painful, and although she later apologized, the damage was done. I left early and was hurt. Even after we cleared things up, this experience taught me that first impressions can be very difficult to undo once someone’s feelings are hurt.

Moreover, first impressions can even change people themselves. For instance, I once shared my negative opinion about my best friend’s boyfriend after seeing him kiss another girl at school. I told her that he didn’t love her, but she accused me of jealousy because she thought he was the most handsome guy around. Nonetheless, I saw his true intentions as someone who enjoyed playing with girls’ feelings. As a result, my friend started avoiding me and stopped talking to me altogether. Later, I found out that the boy had a twin brother, which meant my first impression was completely wrong. I tried to apologize, but she was too hurt and angry. This misunderstanding permanently affected our friendship, and now we speak very little. This example demonstrates how first impressions can affect not only others but also change relationships and people’s behavior.

Some might argue that first impressions can be fixed quickly because they don’t matter much or that others don’t pay attention to them. However, this is rarely the case. People often feel hurt when they receive negative first impressions, which can cause deep emotional changes. Even when problems seem small, first impressions are very hard to reverse once the damage is done.

In conclusion, first impressions are almost impossible to change because once words are said, they cannot easily be taken back. Correcting mistakes or unintended comments is difficult, and sometimes, even a sincere apology is not enough to heal the hurt caused. Since people are sensitive and may hold onto their feelings, first impressions can deeply affect relationships and cause changes in people. For these reasons, first impressions are extremely hard to alter.

It can also be a bad trait because you can be overconfident and cocky. Some people don’t like those kinds of people because they say "they’re no fun" or they are "party poopers." I'll confess that I was a little cocky and overconfident when it came to sports because I was a very competitive kid. Sometimes I even screamed and yelled out of happiness because I scored or won a game. Some people also think our character traits are influenced beyond our control, and yes, I can see their point of view. When I screamed and yelled after I scored or won a game, I didn’t control it; I just yelled. I could have not yelled and just celebrated with my hands raised and looked up at the sky, but I didn’t do that. This is why I think we can choose our character traits like being over yourself.

Finally, I think when the British naturalist and politician John Lubbock wrote, "Your character will be what you yourself choose to make it," he considered two possibilities. He thought we either choose our character traits, or our character forms by influences beyond our control. I think he believed we choose our character traits like being quiet, being social, and being over yourself. This is why I think he believed we choose our character traits.

John Lubbock, a British naturalist and politician, once said, "Your character will be what you yourself choose to make it." This raises the question: do we have control over our character traits, or are they shaped by forces beyond our influence? I believe that we do have the power to choose our character traits, such as being quiet, outgoing, or confident. This is why I am convinced that our character is something we actively shape ourselves.

For instance, being quiet is a trait we can decide to adopt. Being quiet is neither inherently good nor bad; sometimes it is appropriate to remain silent, but at other times, speaking up is necessary. It is important to find a balance. When I was in middle school, between sixth and seventh grade, I was a very quiet student with few friends because I rarely engaged in conversation. I often felt isolated. Later, I made an effort to speak more and gradually made many friends. This experience showed me that our character traits, like being quiet, can be consciously changed.

Another example is being sociable. Being outgoing is beneficial because talking with others can help you make friends, gain knowledge, and explore new experiences. During seventh and eighth grade, I was very talkative, and sometimes I worried that I annoyed others because I talked so much. However, I learned how to approach people and communicate effectively. I also discovered that people can change over time: some who were kind became moody, some who were unpleasant became nicer, and some remained the same. This taught me that we can consciously develop traits like sociability by choosing how we interact with others.

Lastly, consider the trait of being confident or self-assured. Having confidence is a positive quality, but it can turn into arrogance if taken too far. Some people dislike those who are too confident, calling them “party poopers” or saying they are not fun to be around. I admit that I used to be a bit cocky, especially in sports, since I was very competitive. Sometimes I would shout loudly when I scored or won, expressing my excitement without much control. Although some might argue that certain actions are beyond our control, I believe that even in these moments, we can learn to regulate how we express ourselves. This example supports the idea that we have the ability to choose how confident or “over ourselves” we want to be.

In conclusion, when John Lubbock wrote, "Your character will be what you yourself choose to make it," he probably meant that while external influences exist, ultimately, we have the power to shape our own character traits. Whether it is being quiet, sociable, or confident, I believe that we are the architects of our own personalities.

This idea divides people's minds into two camps, two ideologies: cautious, safety-oriented individuals and bold, risk-takers. Both sides have advantages and disadvantages.

Failure is something we all try to avoid in our everyday lives. Many people do their best to stay away from situations where they might fail, while a smaller group chooses to confront failure head-on. These individuals view failure as a chance to learn and often achieve great things as a result.

Fear influences almost every part of our lives. We worry about how others perceive us and if our decisions are correct. Often, our fear of failure stems from uncertainty about whether we will succeed or what the consequences of our actions might be. This fear divides people into two groups: those who play it safe and those who take risks. Each approach has its own advantages and disadvantages.

People who prefer safety tend to rely on their existing knowledge, which they have built up over many years, to avoid failure. Calling them shy isn’t entirely accurate—especially when it comes to new and unfamiliar experiences. They avoid taking risks, and as a result, they usually do not fail because they never attempt the challenge in the first place. This could apply to many situations, such as answering a question in class, trying a new sport, going to the gym, or wearing something different. The main barrier for them is fear. They avoid risks and, in doing so, remain uncertain of outcomes. If they do fail, they accept it as a loss. One possible positive aspect of this mindset is that they do not lose anything by avoiding risks, but their chances for success also tend to be smaller. This doesn’t mean they are always risk-averse or fearful; rather, they prefer safer options. Often, their reluctance is based on past experiences—like saying something awkward in class and being laughed at, or struggling with a sport or feeling uncomfortable at the gym because they were less strong than others.

On the other hand, those who embrace new experiences and learn from them often achieve lasting success. A prime example is Winston Churchill, the former British Prime Minister. His life highlights the importance of trying despite setbacks. Achieving his position was far from easy—his biography details numerous failures he faced before succeeding. People like Churchill see failure as a valuable part of learning. For them, mistakes are opportunities to improve ideas, decisions, and actions. If they make a wrong move that leads to failure, they confront it and, more importantly, take pride not in the mistake itself, but in the lessons learned and the knowledge gained. They use these lessons to avoid repeating the same errors. Although they might fail again at times, in the end, they are the ones who succeed. This is where enthusiasm plays a key role.

Enthusiasm drives people toward their goals. Churchill’s determination to lead his country during World War II shows how a strong purpose can overcome failure. Enthusiasm can take many forms, such as the sense of duty felt by a leader, the joy a musician experiences, or the desire of a parent to bring happiness to their child. Keeping enthusiasm alive depends on the individual, not the size of the goal. Whether the objective is large or small makes little difference. What truly matters is the person’s dedication. Anyone can aim to become a president if they really want it, but going to the gym a few times a week requires personal motivation and willingness. Enthusiasm connects closely with our life goals, whether short-term or long-term. It can weaken after failure or grow even stronger.

A personal example I can share involves learning martial arts. I trained to dual wield the nunchaku, which was very challenging because I am right-handed and had to develop skill in my left hand. The process was painful—my forearm was bruised and sore from repeated mistakes. People asked why I didn’t give up, but my enthusiasm to master the nunchaku kept me going. After months of hard work, I finally succeeded. I am not a master yet, but at least now I rarely hurt myself.

Some people experience failure so many times that they risk reaching a point where trying again becomes impossible—sometimes due to serious consequences like injury or death. These cases are extreme, but failure can take other forms as well. For example, a boy who loved riding his bicycle had a terrible accident and lost a leg. After months in a wheelchair and with the help of a prosthetic, he worked hard in recovery. Although he struggled and was frustrated by repeated failures, he never gave up. Eventually, he was able to ride his bike again and perform tricks just as before. His story is inspiring.

I agree with Winston Churchill’s view that failure is necessary for learning and appreciating success. We should practice not until we simply get things right, but until we cannot get them wrong. Having a goal fuels enthusiasm, which can grow even stronger after every setback. We can choose to stay in our comfort zones, avoiding failure, or we can face failure and gain valuable experience.

Exceptions could be made for events like parties, but there should still be reasonable limits and consequences that start with warnings before becoming stricter.

This is a downside since it could have lasting effects from what might have been a minor mistake.

Overall, these curfews help teenagers avoid trouble and support their growth in multiple important ways.

In some cultures, students are expected to choose a career path by the time they begin high school. The important question is whether it is beneficial for young students to commit to a specific career at such an early stage in their lives.

Deciding on a career early can be advantageous, especially for those interested in professions that require long periods of study, such as medicine, law, teaching, or pediatrics. Starting these courses at a young age can help build a strong foundation and contribute positively to the future development of the country.

Additionally, beginning a career path early provides more chances for students to pursue further opportunities within their chosen field. For instance, a young teacher might decide to change careers later on, and because they started early, they still have the time and energy to pursue a new profession.

However, there are also drawbacks to deciding on a career too soon. Young students might become tired or overwhelmed by their studies, and later in life, they might regret their initial choice upon realizing that they are not passionate about that career.

In conclusion, committing to a career at a young age can be a very good idea for students. Therefore, it is important to encourage and support them in their decisions. It would also be beneficial if teachers and counselors helped students to discover the right career path for their future.

In this essay, I will discuss how the world pressures us to change every day, how we are influenced by these forces and gradually transform, and how each passing year seems to make our generation face more challenges.

Every day, the world looks for ways to make us conform. As individuals, we rarely stop to reflect on what we truly want for our future. Why would anyone want to be just like the crowd? Do I want to be wealthy according to society’s standards? Do I want to achieve my personal dreams? These are the important questions we should ask ourselves and think about carefully. Where will following the path of the majority lead us? Success requires being authentic because the world will not do the work for us.

We are heavily influenced by the world around us—in how we behave, speak, dress, and even in our beliefs. There are many aspects of life where if we don’t follow what’s popular or expected, we are considered uncool or out of place. For example, the clothes we wear often determine how society views us. If we don’t wear trendy or popular brands, we might be seen as less likable. Sometimes, this is not because we don’t want to keep up but because we lack the money, time, or access to get them, or simply because we prefer different styles. Unfortunately, this leads to people being bullied or even developing depression because they don’t fit in, which is truly sad.

Sadly, with each year that passes, our generation seems to be facing more problems, and the world’s negative influence plays a big role in this. We see the rise of drug addiction, conflicts between nations, and music that often glorifies violence, drugs, and sex. These influences can have harmful effects on young people today. If we don’t learn to be ourselves and set positive examples, the future could be very bleak.

Some argue that the world itself is bad and only brings negative influences, but I believe that’s not entirely true. It is often us who allow ourselves to be affected by bad habits and then blame the world for our problems. Ultimately, it is our responsibility to choose what we get involved in. I hope that the world can change because there is still time to make a difference. I also wish for the upcoming generation to have the strength and determination to transform the world into a better, kinder place.

My father was very upset and searched for a job for almost three months without success. During this hard time, my mother comforted him by saying, "Don’t worry, we will overcome this like we always do. I’m here to support you." Her words quickly lifted his spirits. He smiled at her and thanked her for believing in him. Then he took the car keys and set out to find a new job. Eventually, he found a position that paid better than his previous one, and our financial problems disappeared.

Believing in yourself is not always easy. At times, it can be hard to understand your own abilities, but there is often someone kind who helps you recognize your strength and what you can achieve. When I was in tenth grade, my algebra teacher constantly encouraged us to believe more in ourselves. Many students struggled because they did not understand the subject, and a lot of us became disappointed and didn't even try to complete the tasks. In the first quarter, many of us failed. We thought our grades would never improve. However, our teacher spoke with us and inspired us to have faith in our abilities. Gradually, we changed our attitude—not because we wanted to at first, but because she helped us believe that we could succeed. By the end of the second quarter, many students had improved their grades from around 50 to 90. This happened because we started paying attention, believing in ourselves, and attempting tasks even when they seemed difficult. I am still grateful to that teacher because she not only helped us improve our grades but also taught us to be confident. Sometimes we made her upset due to our lack of belief in ourselves, but she never gave up on us. She became one of the best teachers and friends to me and many classmates, always supporting and encouraging us. This experience showed me how vital a positive attitude is in life.

Our attitude should remain positive even during the toughest times. Some people think that a positive attitude is only necessary during important or happy moments, but this is mistaken. We need to maintain a positive outlook at all times to succeed in life and experience happiness. In families, older members such as grandparents, parents, and siblings should lead by example so that children learn confidence and positivity from them.

In conclusion, having a positive attitude is essential for success and happiness in life. It helps us overcome difficulties, supports those around us, and allows us to believe in ourselves no matter what challenges we face.

The program that allows students to attend classes online can have both positive and negative effects. Different schools handle this option in various ways; some offer online classes, while others do not. People also have differing opinions about online learning. Some believe it is a great idea, while others think it is not beneficial. One advantage of online classes is that students can work at their own pace without waiting for others. However, there are downsides too, such as unreliable internet connections, difficulties in completing assignments, lack of interaction with peers of the same age, and sometimes neglecting to complete tasks.

Students taking classes online may struggle to finish their assignments. They might not be able to ask questions when they face difficulties and have to solve problems independently. Many educational websites may not provide accurate answers, leading students to make mistakes on their work. Although there are videos available online to help with learning, sometimes the specific topics a student needs are not covered. In a traditional classroom, teachers can explain difficult concepts, which helps students understand better. Online classes often lack immediate access to teachers when students need help. Additionally, some students might not manage their time well and fail to submit assignments promptly, choosing to delay work and sometimes never completing it at all. Thus, meeting deadlines can be a real challenge in an online learning environment.

Being around peers of the same age helps students develop study habits and receive support. In contrast, online schooling usually means working alone on a computer, without classmates to collaborate or discuss with. Even if students have friends, they might not share the same classes, making group study difficult. Online learners might also have fewer opportunities to socialize and make new friends since they often spend time working or doing other activities with older people or alone. A traditional classroom provides a social setting where students learn better by interacting with others their age. With online classes, students miss out on this valuable social environment and can feel isolated.

Another issue with online classes is that sometimes a lot of assignments are due on the same day. This can be overwhelming, especially if students do not fully understand the material or find it hard to keep up with the workload. Completing assignments is crucial for understanding the subject, but some students might simply search the internet for answers that look similar and copy them without truly learning. Procrastination is also a common problem, with students delaying their work until the last moment. This laziness can lead to poor grades, failing the class, and having to retake it. Furthermore, distractions from home or other parts of life can prevent students from focusing on their studies. Not doing the work on time can ultimately harm their progress and prevent them from finishing the course successfully.

Schools offer different methods for attending classes, such as online programs or traditional in-person lessons. These options can help students attend more classes and possibly free up some time. However, some students might misuse the opportunity to stay home and avoid studying. Life can sometimes present unexpected challenges, and not having a teacher available when help is needed can make learning even harder. In the end, students must decide what works best for them. While online classes offer flexibility, they can also bring difficulties like lack of interaction with peers and struggling to complete assignments. For many students, online learning does not always lead to success.

There has long been a debate about whether it is better to work alone or as part of a group. Many people and experts agree that working with others offers greater advantages.

One key reason for this is that being in a group brings together different perspectives, ideas, and ways of thinking, which can be very helpful when facing difficulties. For instance, when organizing something large like a school event or something smaller such as a classroom presentation, you might sometimes run out of ideas. In these situations, you can rely on your team to provide a variety of solutions, whereas working solo might feel like being stuck in a dead-end.

Working in a group can also create a more relaxed and positive atmosphere, even during stressful or challenging moments. When collaborating with others, you rarely experience boredom because there is always something to discuss. Additionally, you and your teammates share memories that can later become a source of laughter and enjoyment.

Another benefit of teamwork is that tasks can be completed more quickly. Having multiple people working together allows the project to progress faster than if one person were doing everything alone. This efficiency also leaves room for creativity, enabling you to refine details or come up with new ideas.

Being part of a team shifts your mindset from focusing on "I" to thinking about "we." This outlook is valuable for the future when dealing with different personalities and viewpoints in the real world. Developing teamwork skills becomes an important part of personal growth and preparation for various situations.

When the group finishes a project, everyone often feels a strong sense of achievement. This shared pride can motivate members to keep working hard and never give up.

Although working in a group might sometimes seem complicated or challenging, it offers chances to gain new experiences and develop skills. It helps build character and personal growth by teaching you how to communicate effectively and express your ideas clearly. For all these reasons, many people believe that collaborating with others is more beneficial than working alone.

Winston Churchill, the former Prime Minister of Britain, once remarked that "success is going from failure to failure without losing enthusiasm."

Many individuals with ambitions and dreams would agree with this idea.

Failure, when seen as part of the journey to success, can provide motivation, encourage reflection for improvement, and offer valuable experience.

Failure doesn’t always have to be negative.

For many people, failure acts as the push they need to keep going. When students fail once, they often realize the importance of rising again and trying harder. Would most individuals simply give up after failing just once? Imagine someone aiming for a very high goal who encounters failure along the way; they must accept that setbacks are inevitable in such a pursuit. When failure comes, it should inspire motivation rather than defeat. Without this drive, no one would be able to achieve their dreams. For example, consider a student who spends an entire night preparing for a test, confident in their performance, but then discovers they didn’t do as well as expected. Fortunately, there is often a chance to retake tests. Sometimes, things don’t go as planned, but that doesn’t mean success is impossible—it just means one must continue trying.

Another reason failure can lead to success is that it encourages people to think about how to improve. The common saying, "You learn from your mistakes," holds true. When an effort fails due to mistakes, people tend to reflect on what went wrong to avoid repeating the same errors. This process of learning and improving is essential in moving closer to success. Knowing where to begin and what to change is a vital part of achieving goals. Many successful individuals admit that they had to face several failures before reaching their current position.

Lastly, failure provides valuable experience. Without encountering failure, there wouldn’t be the lessons needed for future challenges. The experience gained from failing helps when tackling the next objective. Achieving success after overcoming failure creates a powerful story—one that includes the obstacles faced and the determination to continue despite setbacks. Sharing such experiences can inspire others who may also have failed but feel like giving up, showing them that failure does not mean success is unattainable.

In summary, failure can serve as an important step toward success if approached correctly. Instead of giving up, people should see failure as a chance to gain motivation, think about improvement, and gain experience. In this way, failure becomes a valuable and even positive part of the path to achievement.

Summer is a season characterized by very hot weather, and schools use this entire period to give students a significant break. The summer vacation lasts for nearly two months. Although some educators believe that the summer break is too lengthy and suggest switching to year-round schooling—with a shorter summer break of one month and a longer winter break—I disagree with this idea. I believe schools should not operate year-round because the intense heat during summer makes attending school difficult, and students need this time to plan trips with their family and friends.

The extremely hot weather in summer makes it hard for students to concentrate in class. On some days, temperatures can reach 96°C or higher, which is too hot for students to handle comfortably. Such high temperatures cause excessive sweating and headaches, making it difficult for students to focus during lessons. The heat can also increase levels of irritability and stress, leading to poor academic performance or frustration. Students who work in hot conditions experience even greater challenges compared to those in milder climates. The heat reduces concentration and makes completing tasks much harder.

During the two-month summer break, students have the opportunity to enjoy time with their families and go on trips. Many students and their families plan long vacations during this period. They look forward to this time of year to visit the beach, travel to other countries, or simply spend quality time together. Since there are no school days in summer, students don’t miss out on lessons while traveling. Trips often take a lot of time, and summer is an ideal period to relax and explore new places. Additionally, some students use their summer holidays to find temporary jobs. Without school commitments, they can focus on earning money. Therefore, summer break is essential for students to rest, spend time with family, or gain work experience.

In conclusion, summer is a challenging time to attend school because of the hot weather, but it is also a valuable break for travel and work. The government should not shorten this important vacation. Summer is our well-deserved break—a special time to relax after a year of hard work at school. It happens only once each year, and students should be able to fully enjoy it.

Nowadays, with all the benefits of technology, people tend to exercise less and move less frequently. For example, we often use cars to go everywhere, so we walk less. We do not even have to walk over to talk to someone—we just send a text message. Even to find out the weather, we don’t need to get up; we can simply check our phones. Technology has reached a point where if we don't want to go to the cinema, we can just stay home and watch movies or shows on Netflix, Hulu, Disney, or other apps.

While these advances are convenient, they also make people more inactive and prone to gaining weight, which leads to more health issues like heart attacks and high cholesterol.

If things continue this way without any changes, the situation will only become worse in the future.

One way to help future students, like those at this school, is to teach them that there are healthier food options beyond fast food. Healthy foods can taste great and some might even be better than unhealthy options—for example, avocado, fruit juices, Caesar salad, and fish. These types of food can help create a balance between what our bodies need to function well and what we want to eat.

A good method of introducing these new options is through the school menu. It could include foods that children have never tried before and that contain less fat than something like pizza.

This would mean that as they grow older, they won’t only look for hamburgers, Chinese food, or chicken wings. Instead, they will be aware of other choices that can benefit their health.

If we don’t encourage these habits now, it will be much harder to get them to adopt healthy eating habits later on.

From my point of view, as a member of this school community concerned about my future and that of my classmates, I believe adding healthier choices to the school cafeteria menu would be a great idea for everyone. After all, we don’t want to face health problems because of what we eat.

Technology enables individuals to accomplish many tasks without interacting face-to-face with others.

People can borrow books, make purchases, or enjoy games without having a conversation with someone else.

But has this reduction in human contact caused by technology brought positive or negative consequences to our lives?

I believe that relying too much on technology and the resulting lack of real communication will harm our social connections.

This problem will become more serious as smartphones and other devices continue to develop.

In the future, technology might dominate how humans live and relate to each other.

For example, imagine a boy and a girl from school who initially communicate only through social media. One day, they decide to meet in person. Although their first meeting feels awkward, they quickly become close friends. They start hanging out together—going to the movies, shopping at the mall, dining at restaurants, and so on.

They move from being strangers to becoming a couple. This kind of relationship is very meaningful because loving someone deeply goes beyond physical actions; it means being there for each other and sharing support.

Finding that special person is truly a gift. Many people struggle to express their feelings in person, while admitting emotions over a screen feels easier. But is it always genuine?

Saying "I love you" sincerely means a great deal, and hearing it multiple times can be heartwarming. However, sometimes people only say things through devices without true commitment. Likewise, breaking up by text shows a lack of courage to face the other person honestly. I think everyone should at least try to communicate honestly in person, to experience the fullness of life beyond just being glued to their phones.

One day, if this trend continues, people might even destroy their phones to avoid becoming controlled by technology like robots.

By coming together as a community, we can challenge this obsession with phones and electronic devices and prevent it from taking over our lives. Opening up to someone face-to-face is like watching a flower bloom. Meeting that special person in reality brings happiness and connection.

Overall, the decline in real human interaction caused by technology has negative effects on people’s lives. I believe that someday we will reunite as humans and overcome this issue together.

Group work allows us to collaborate and exchange ideas, makes tasks more fun and manageable, and gives us the opportunity to interact with people we might not usually talk to. Additionally, working in groups helps ensure that projects are completed on time.

One important benefit of working in groups is the ability to share ideas. When we work together, we can combine our thoughts to brainstorm and discuss different perspectives about the project or assignment. This collaboration helps everyone understand the topic better and ensures active participation from all members. By sharing opinions, group members can contribute effectively to the task at hand, which enriches the quality of the work.

Another advantage is that group work helps with organization and meeting deadlines. Working alone can sometimes be difficult and time-consuming, often causing delays or requiring help that is hard to find. On the other hand, groups usually have three or four people, which allows tasks to be divided and completed more quickly. Assigning specific roles to each member helps streamline the work process and supports the group’s goal to finish the assignment on time.

Finally, working in groups can be enjoyable and easier because it enables social interaction with classmates we might not know well. Some individuals prefer working alone to avoid socializing, which is alright, but I find group work both fun and beneficial. Collaborating with others creates a more relaxed environment where people feel comfortable and open. Sometimes, someone in the group might make a joke or share something funny, which can momentarily distract us but also adds laughter, smiles, and happiness to the experience. This positive atmosphere makes working in groups more exciting.

In conclusion, working in groups offers more benefits than working individually. Groups allow us to exchange ideas, complete tasks on time, and enjoy the process by collaborating with others. Before starting the work, group members discuss and ensure everyone understands the task, which is crucial for success. Group work teaches us the importance of encouraging one another, teamwork, hard work, support, and determination, all of which contribute to achieving better results together.

Technology enables individuals to accomplish many activities without needing to interact directly with others. For instance, people can borrow books, shop online, or play games without having to talk to anyone else. However, technology has both positive and negative impacts on people’s lives. While some argue that technology is beneficial because it can be used in emergencies by everyone, many others believe that it can negatively influence people's behavior and lead them to value virtual connections more than real-life relationships.

Some people support the idea that technology is helpful, especially in urgent situations. Imagine a family living in a remote area with no neighbors nearby. In such cases, technology becomes essential for their survival. For example, when I lived in my country, many families lived far from the city and some did not have any devices to keep in touch with others. Those families often faced difficult circumstances, especially when someone fell ill and couldn't get immediate help, sometimes leading to tragic outcomes. This shows how crucial technology can be during emergencies.

On the other hand, many believe technology negatively affects people's behavior and attitudes. In 1978, for example, people were generally more respectful to one another, even if they had little education. Today, many claim that movies, music, novels, and cartoons influence a person’s behavior through technology. It is true that excessive use of technology can cause mental health issues or create a kind of dependence. For instance, I know a family with a fifteen-year-old girl who watches a lot of TV shows. She behaves as if she is older than her peers and often disrespects her parents. Her behavior is problematic, but her parents continue to provide her with many technological gadgets without monitoring their use. Allowing children easy access to technology at a young age can be harmful; some kids do not use it responsibly, and as they grow up, parents lose control and children may adopt bad habits learned from technology. Instead of relying on devices, parents should spend time with their children and engage with them directly.

Moreover, many people think technology is harmful because it causes individuals to prioritize screens over the people around them. It is true that many spend much of their time focused on devices. Psychologist Generic_Name said, “It is better to have face-to-face conversations because people can understand situations more clearly,” and this is accurate, since people can easily deceive others behind a screen. Nowadays, companies produce more and more devices that make people overly absorbed in technology. Studies show that nearly ninety percent of people pay more attention to their devices than to their family or those nearby. For example, about five months ago, I read a book called "Behind the Wed," which tells the story of a female teacher communicating with someone online whom she did not know. When they were doing public school, they were failing their classes, or the problems they were facing made it harder for them to be in school. Many students have done online school and have been very successful. Not only have they been successful, but it has also benefited them in whatever situation they're in right now.

Although some may argue otherwise, I have seen the benefits through family experiences, podcasts I've listened to on the radio, and from hearing some celebrities talk.

One of my cousins named Generic_Name has been through so much and has not been able to continue going to public school. She's struggling a lot to keep her grades up and get to school on time. She has an eating disorder, which can be really hard to deal with alongside school. Her family decided to let her do online school, and it has helped her so much. While being at home, eating, and going to doctor appointments, she has the option to do her assignments online. Sometimes teachers even come to her house to help with homework assignments, which helps her a ton. Through online school, she has overcome her struggle with her eating disorder and has been very successful. As the years went by, she studied more and more. "It's so crazy," because despite all the problems she was facing, she became a lawyer.

Some may argue that it's impossible for her to have become a lawyer after just doing online school. They say it's unfair that she got to where she is because of homeschooling. Some people may say that doing online school cannot benefit you or make you successful; it’s just a path to failure. That's not true. When you hear so many stories and people talking about their experiences with homeschooling, you have to consider that maybe it helps some and not others.

Many podcasts on the radio have mentioned real-life situations on this subject. One that stood out to me was when a mom talked about her son, Generic_Name, who is really popular on social media. She said that throughout his high school years, students his age and older bullied him and tried to get into fights with him for no reason. The mom signed her son up for online schooling. Generic_Name did online school and had video conferences with his teachers every other day. Generic_Name said he found it easier because it was just him and his laptop with no distractions or students bothering him or trying to fight him. Since social media is such a big part of life, doing online school allows him to keep up with social media and be educated at the same time. However, some may argue that Generic_Name has to be a man and grow up; he can’t always hide from mean people. That’s true; he can't always hide from people like that. But if he's fed up with it, maybe online school was the best decision, as you can only handle so much hate.

Celebrities have spoken in interviews about choosing homeschool over public school and how beneficial it was. There’s a girl named Generic_Name who said being big on social media is really hard. She dealt with hate, people exposing her constantly for no reason, and her name always being in people’s mouths. Generic_Name said she was bullied many times and found it harder to deal with. At one point, she developed depression, and it became harder and harder to continue going to public schools. Teachers recommended she do online school. She took that advice and did homeschooling for the rest of high school and online school for college as well. She said she feels more successful. Generic_Name said online school was the best thing she did. She also decided that for college she would attend a public college and continue being big on social media. Some may argue they don’t see how it benefited her, questioning if it made a major change since she already knew what she wanted to do. It benefited her in many ways; she no longer fears what people think of her on social media. Sometimes people need space from public school, and when they feel ready, they can return.

The important thing is for people going through the same problems to look at and learn from past experiences. They can see if online school is beneficial for them. In the future, people can look back at this and see what others were going through and how much they struggled. This helps compare the past to the present. A solution is for people to do online school if they feel that public school is harder for them or for whatever reason. Also, people should notice and realize that, as said multiple times, those who are big on social media find it hard to cope with all the hate they receive. A solution is for people not to give hate to others.

Have you ever wondered whether attending classes from home truly benefits students? Many young people strive to get an education and achieve success, but various challenges often make traditional public or private schools less suitable for them. As a result, some choose to pursue their studies online and report that it has greatly helped them. For many, attending public school had led to failing grades or increased difficulties, but switching to online education has allowed them to thrive despite their circumstances.

Although some might disagree, my perspective is based on personal family experiences, radio podcasts, and comments from famous individuals.

For example, my cousin, whom I will call Generic_Name, faced numerous struggles that prevented her from continuing with public school. She had trouble maintaining good grades and getting to school on time, all while battling an eating disorder. Managing this condition alongside school was extremely tough. Her family decided that online education would be better for her. Studying at home enabled her to recover as she could eat properly and attend medical appointments while still completing her assignments. Sometimes, teachers even visited her at home to offer extra support. Thanks to online schooling, she overcame her disorder and became very successful. Over the years, she dedicated herself to her studies and, incredibly, eventually became a lawyer.

Some people claim that becoming a lawyer through online schooling is improbable or unfair. They argue that online education cannot lead to success and might only bring failure. However, numerous stories and personal testimonies prove that it can be beneficial for some individuals, even if it is not the right path for everyone.

I have listened to various podcasts on this topic, including one where a mother discussed her son, Generic_Name, who is popular on social media. Throughout his school years, he was frequently bullied and faced unfair confrontations with other students. To protect him, his mother enrolled him in online school. He participated in video conferences with teachers every other day and found studying much easier without the distractions or threats present in a traditional classroom. In addition, online schooling allowed him to balance his education with maintaining his social media presence. Some may argue that he should toughen up and face bullies instead of avoiding them. While resilience is important, sometimes stepping away from constant harassment is the best choice for someone’s well-being.

Many celebrities have also spoken about choosing homeschooling and online education to manage their own challenges. One young woman, also named Generic_Name, described how being famous on social media exposed her to constant negativity and bullying. This affected her mental health and led to depression, making it increasingly difficult to continue attending public school. Following her teachers’ advice, she switched to homeschooling for high school and later completed college online. She feels that this decision greatly improved her life, and she plans to attend a public college while continuing her social media career. Some critics question how online schooling helped her when she already knew her ambitions. However, it gave her the freedom to recover emotionally and build confidence without fear of judgment. Sometimes, taking a break from public school is necessary, and students can return when they are ready.

It is important for those facing similar difficulties to learn from these stories and consider whether online education might be helpful for them. Understanding past experiences helps people see how challenges have been managed and overcome over time. Online schooling can be a valuable solution for anyone finding traditional school too overwhelming or unsuitable. Additionally, it’s crucial to recognize the struggles faced by those active on social media and to reduce the amount of hate directed at others.

Overall, online education offers real benefits to many students, enabling them to succeed despite personal hardships and external pressures. It is an option worth considering for anyone who feels that conventional schooling is not meeting their needs.

I strongly believe that attending classes from home does not offer any real advantages to students. I will explain three main reasons to support this view. First, students often fail to learn effectively by the end of the semester when studying online. Second, they are easily distracted and find it hard to concentrate on their lessons. Lastly, learning is much more efficient when a teacher is physically present in front of students.

To start, if students sometimes struggle to learn even in a classroom setting, it is even harder for them to focus in front of a computer screen at home. When studying remotely, students tend to rush through their work just to finish quickly so they can move on to other activities. This lack of engagement leads to disinterest in the lessons, and when it comes time to demonstrate their knowledge, they often feel unprepared. For example, I personally find that the glare from the computer screen makes it difficult to concentrate.

Furthermore, being at home makes it very easy for students to become distracted. Online classes give access to many electronic devices such as phones, TVs, and even the computer itself, which can divert their attention. There are also distractions from family members; for instance, if parents ask a student to watch younger siblings, the student cannot fully focus on studying. Compared to friends causing disruptions in school, distractions at home can be even more challenging, especially since many young people have friends who play video games nearby.

Finally, learning is more effective when it takes place in a classroom where students can see and interact with their teacher directly. For example, I enjoy discussing topics with both my teacher and classmates because it helps me understand the material better and hear different perspectives. Being physically present allows students to absorb the information more effectively, whereas studying alone on a computer often causes the material to be forgotten shortly after.

In conclusion, learning in a classroom with face-to-face interaction is the best way for students to gain the knowledge they need to succeed. Online classes at home often result in poor academic performance due to distractions and lack of engagement. Attending school is not only about lessons but also about social interaction and acquiring skills necessary for life beyond academics. Overall, being in a classroom environment is more convenient and effective for obtaining a proper education.

For instance, a student with arthritis might find it difficult to physically attend school, so online classes or video chats with a tutor would allow them to continue their education comfortably. This way, they can access all the courses they need and work toward earning a diploma, which is important for their future. Moreover, home learning can benefit students who have had difficulties at school, such as conflicts with other students. These individuals can receive support and continue learning in a more peaceful environment without attending school in person.

On the other hand, I feel that learning from home may not be a positive experience for students who simply do not want to go to school. Without a teacher present to guide them, these students might not stay focused and may miss important explanations, leading to poor understanding. Many students who are still learning English do not want to attend school but want to improve their language skills. For example, since I am not a native English speaker, if I chose to study at home, it would be harder for me to learn because I would not be exposed to English as much as I am at school. At school, I can hear and practice English throughout the day, and I have friends who can help me. Attending school has helped me improve my language skills even though it is challenging. The support of teachers and classmates makes a big difference.

In conclusion, studying from home is not entirely beneficial for every student. While it has advantages for some, it can be difficult for others who do not learn as well without being in a school setting. Whether learning at home or at school, the important thing is to have the motivation to study and succeed. For me, going to school is essential for improving my life each day, gaining new knowledge, and building confidence with the help of teachers and peers.

Picture a world that feels dull, gloomy, and lifeless, filled with people struggling with depression. This bleak scenario might come true if everyone believes that small acts of kindness make no difference.

However, these simple gestures can actually have a powerful impact on the world and help improve it. One important benefit is that kindness helps build a good reputation. There are many ways to gain respect, but being kind to those around you is one of the easiest and most effective. Showing kindness can strengthen any relationship, and often leads others to respond with kindness in return. From my own experience, I’ve noticed that even a brief compliment can brighten someone’s day. Likewise, when I’m feeling down, others often show me kindness, which really lifts my spirits. Being known for kindness makes you stand out; people will remember you as the nicest person around, and they may seek your positivity through compliments or friendly gestures.

Another significant advantage of kindness is its potential to improve communities and even the entire world. Our society faces many problems, but kindness could help reduce negativity. When you treat someone kindly, it not only makes them happy but encourages them to spread that kindness to others, creating a positive cycle. The more people act kindly, the wider this ripple effect grows, influencing many to do the same. I have seen this happen in my own school—when I made an effort to be kind to those around me, others noticed and started being nicer too. This way, kindness becomes contagious, and everyone benefits.

Lastly, kindness can truly uplift others and improve their self-esteem. As Aesop famously said, “No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.” A simple compliment can change someone’s entire day, and the warmth of kindness often extends beyond the immediate person to those nearby. Kindness has the power to change lives; it certainly changed mine. When I was about eleven years old, I faced difficulties at school and at home, but the friends I made through small acts of kindness helped transform my year—and perhaps even my life—because I knew they would support me for a long time. Being kind to people who are struggling can provide the support they need to find more happiness in their lives.

All these reasons show that even the smallest act of kindness can make a meaningful difference in someone's life.

This essay aims to examine the pros and cons of implementing a four-day school week with ten-hour days. Some people believe this schedule could help save energy and resources.

As a student, I agree that a shorter school week might offer some benefits, but I do not support extending each school day by two hours. For many students, spending eight hours in school is already a lot since sitting in class for long periods can be very tiring. For example, there is often at least one student in every class who falls asleep during lessons due to the heavy workload, after-school jobs, or sports commitments. These factors make it hard for some students to stay alert. Adding two more hours to the school day just to gain a three-day weekend might seem appealing, but it does not really help overall.

Extending the school day by two hours over four days still uses the same amount of energy that would have been spent during the regular five-day week. To illustrate, the extra two hours from Monday to Thursday add up to eight hours, which balances out the one day off. This means there is no actual energy saving happening, despite what some might think.

For instance, my friend Generic_Name enjoys the idea of a four-day week because it gives him an extra day to do homework and spend time with his girlfriend. For him, this change is clearly advantageous.

On the other hand, my boyfriend Generic_Name does not agree with this idea. Although he loves studying, he has two hours of basketball practice after school and then works for about four hours to help his mother pay for car insurance. This schedule leaves him with very little time to rest or complete homework. Many students are in similar situations, balancing family responsibilities with schoolwork, and longer days would only increase their exhaustion.

We should also consider the opinions of teachers, who would have to teach for ten hours straight. They are not machines, and such a demanding schedule might be hard for them as well. They may not support extending school hours just to shorten the week.

In conclusion, my school should avoid adopting this four-day, ten-hour day model because decisions need to benefit everyone—students, teachers, and staff alike. We cannot be certain this system will work well in our school community. Although some businesses have successfully used similar schedules, schools are different environments with unique activities and challenges, so what works for companies may not suit our educational setting.
